motivation: Existing reduction techniques mainly target second-order Ising models, but many optimization problems naturally contain higher-order interactions, leading to combinatorial explosion.
method: The authors generalize non-separable groups to arbitrary-order Ising-like Hamiltonians and develop an iterative reduction framework that detects and merges constrained spin groups into single variables.
result: The reduction is benchmarked on synthetic hypergraphs and higher-order network datasets, showing effective problem size reduction when integrated with downstream solvers.
conclusion: The framework establishes a foundation for Hamiltonian reduction in higher-order Ising-like optimization problems, potentially improving solver efficiency.

title: Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Physics From The Hubbard Model: A Floquet-Engineering Approach
authors: Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, and Nathan Goldman

Ultracold atoms in an optical lattice could emulate a prominent model of quantum matter linked to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046302] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The SYK model is a prominent model of quantum matter with connections to black holes and high-Tc superconductivity, but its experimental realization is challenging. The authors aim to provide a feasible platform using ultracold atoms.
method: They use Floquet engineering with periodic driving to generate the necessary all-to-all interactions and disorder in a Hubbard model, simulating the SYK model.
result: The approach yields the characteristic SYK physics, including emergent conformal symmetry and maximal chaos, as verified by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a practical route to experimentally study the SYK model and its connections to quantum gravity and condensed matter physics.

title: Diffusion Cascade In A Model Of Interacting Random Walkers
authors: Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Vadim Oganesyan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Vadim Oganesyan

We consider the relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas. Linear hydrodynamics predicts that such perturbations should relax exponentially, but nonlinear effects were predicted to cause subexponential relaxation via nonperturbative long-time tails [L. V. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014312] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subexponential relaxation of density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas due to nonlinear long-time tails.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in interacting many-body systems beyond linear hydrodynamics is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze a facilitated classical lattice gas model using theoretical and numerical methods to compute the relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves.
result: They find that nonlinear effects cause subexponential relaxation via nonperturbative long-time tails, deviating from exponential decay predicted by linear hydrodynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals the importance of nonlinear fluctuations in relaxation dynamics, but the model is classical and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding, focusing on resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: To optimize quantum phase estimation for chemical systems by evaluating different Hamiltonian simulation techniques and basis sets.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other encoding methods in terms of qubit count, gate complexity, and circuit depth for simulating chemical Hamiltonians.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces the number of qubits and gates compared to standard methods, but the overall resource requirements remain high.
conclusion: Sorted-list encoding offers improvements but fault-tolerant quantum simulation of chemical systems still requires significant resources.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Belief propagation (BP) is a heuristic for tensor network contraction that lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to provide systematic corrections to BP that yield polynomial-time algorithms with provable approximation guarantees.
method: The authors develop a cluster expansion framework that adds corrections to BP by considering clusters of tensors, leading to a hierarchy of approximations with exponential convergence in the cluster size.
result: They prove that the cluster-corrected BP algorithm converges exponentially fast to the exact contraction value, with rigorous error bounds, and demonstrate its effectiveness on various tensor network benchmarks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected BP offers a practical and provably accurate method for tensor network contraction, bridging the gap between heuristic BP and exact contraction methods.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a recent theoretical concept with few experimental realizations; cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative many-body system to study it.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform and map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological behavior.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for exploring non-Hermitian topology, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates (T-count) is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation because T gates are costly to implement with error correction. The authors aim to exploit commuting structures in quantum circuits to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli operators to be commuted through T gates simultaneously, enabling more efficient circuit synthesis.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces T-count compared to existing methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for T-count reduction, contributing to the optimization of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper studies the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, providing a combinatorial characterization and bounds based on rank-width.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of graph-state preparation is important for quantum computing and networking, but the paper focuses on circuit complexity rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and characterize graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and elementary edge-complementations. They relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and provide algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
result: For any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(n log n) and at least Ω(r) for connected graphs. Interval and circle graphs have O(n) and O(n log n) CZ-complexity, respectively.
conclusion: The paper provides a combinatorial understanding of graph-state preparation complexity, but it is more aligned with quantum circuit complexity and graph theory than with the core interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Exact Quantum Many-Body Scars In 2d Quantum Gauge Models
authors: Yuan Miao, Linhao Li, Hosho Katsura, And Masahito Yamazaki
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2164 (2026).

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) serve as important examples of ergodicity-breaking phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Despite recent extensive studies, exact QMBS are rare in dimensions higher than one. In this paper, we study a two-dimensional quantum [MATH] gauge model that is dual to a two-dimensional spin-[MATH] XY model defined on bipartite graphs. We identify the exact eigenstates of the XY model with a tower structure as exact QMBS. Exploiting the duality transformation, we show that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) after the transformation are the exact QMBS of the dual [MATH] gauge model. This construction is versatile and has potential applications for finding new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

.
tldr: This paper constructs exact quantum many-body scars in a 2D quantum gauge model via duality to an XY model.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are rare in higher dimensions; the authors aim to provide exact examples in 2D.
method: They study a 2D quantum Z2 gauge model dual to a spin-1/2 XY model on bipartite graphs, identifying exact eigenstates with a tower structure as scars.
result: Exact QMBS are found in the XY model and, via duality, in the gauge model, demonstrating a versatile construction.
conclusion: This work provides new exact QMBS in 2D, with potential for extension to other higher-dimensional models.

title: Machine Learning Decoding Of Circuit-Level Noise For Bivariate Bicycle Codes
authors: John Blue, Harshil Avlani, Zhiyang He, Liu Ziyin, And Isaac L. Chuang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2149 (2026).

Fault-tolerant quantum computers will depend crucially on the performance of the classical decoding algorithm which takes in the results of measurements and outputs corrections to the errors inferred to have occurred. Machine learning models have shown great promise as decoders for the surface code; however, this promise has not yet been substantiated for the more challenging task of decoding quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. In this paper, we present a recurrent, transformer-based neural network designed to decode circuit-level noise on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes. For the [MATH] BB code, at a physical error rate of [MATH], our model achieves logical error rates almost [MATH] times lower than belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding (BP-OSD), and roughly [MATH] times larger than a most-likely error decoder. Moreover, while BP-OSD has a wide distribution of runtimes with significant outliers, our model has a consistent runtime and is an order-of-magnitude faster than the worst-case times from a benchmark BP-OSD implementation. On the [MATH] BB code, our model obtains worse logical error rates but maintains the speed advantage. These results provide initial evidence that machine learning decoders can out-perform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but suggest more complex architectures and/or training procedures are necessary to scale to larger code sizes.

.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning decoding to bivariate bicycle codes, a type of QLDPC code, achieving lower logical error rates and faster runtime than BP-OSD on small codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computers require efficient decoders, and machine learning decoders have shown promise for surface codes but not yet for QLDPC codes, which are more challenging.
method: A recurrent, transformer-based neural network is designed to decode circuit-level noise on bivariate bicycle codes, trained on simulated error data.
result: On the [[144,12,12]] BB code, the ML decoder achieves logical error rates almost 10 times lower than BP-OSD and is an order of magnitude faster, but on the [[288,12,18]] code it performs worse while maintaining speed advantage.
conclusion: Machine learning decoders can outperform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but scaling to larger codes requires more complex architectures or training procedures.

title: High-gain Effects In Broadband Continuous-wave Parametric Down Conversion Sources And Measurements With Undetected Photons
authors: Martin Houde, Franz Roeder, Christine Silberhorn, Benjamin Brecht And Nicolás Quesada
abstract: We study theoretically how high-gain effects affect the measurement outcome of visible signal spectra in undetected photon measurement schemes. We consider two interferometric configurations: firstly, the SU(1,1) interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers; secondly, the induced coherence interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers and where the second squeezer is seeded by the idler and a vacuum ancilla mode. Furthermore, we consider a distributed loss configuration where the idler incurs loss as it propagates in the nonlinear medium. Motivated by experimental evidence and due to the fact that broadband sources are ideal for these measurement schemes, we use the dispersive data of a third-order dispersion engineered integrated waveguide parametric down conversion (PDC) source presented in Roeder et al (2024 New J. Phys. 26 123025) to model the PDC spectra in the three configurations. For each configuration we consider the case of idler-only (i) absorption, (ii) additional dispersion, and (iii) the combined effects. We obtain results which outline the strength and weaknesses of the different configurations at different operation points.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies high-gain effects in broadband continuous-wave parametric down conversion sources for measurements with undetected photons, focusing on interferometric configurations.
motivation: Understanding high-gain effects is important for improving the performance of quantum measurement schemes that rely on undetected photons, which are relevant to quantum imaging and sensing.
method: The authors model parametric down conversion spectra in SU(1,1) and induced coherence interferometers, considering idler loss and dispersion, using dispersive data from an integrated waveguide source.
result: They outline the strengths and weaknesses of different configurations at various operation points, showing how high-gain affects measurement outcomes.
conclusion: The study provides insights into optimizing broadband PDC sources for undetected photon measurements, but the work is primarily about source characterization and interferometry rather than quantum networking.

title: Cavity-induced Multispin Interactions And Phase Transitions In Ultracold Fermi Gases
authors: Shi-Liang Zhu And Z D Wang Zhen Zheng
abstract: The many-body physics of higher-spin systems is expected to host qualitatively new matter phases, but realizing them requires the controllable interactions between multispin components that can be tuned independently for each component. Here we propose a scheme that meets this demand in ultracold Fermi gases. By engineering the atom-cavity coupling, we generate cavity-induced effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. Focusing on the simplest spin-1 case, we obtain two independent scattering channels whose relative strengths and signs are determined by the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical-field parameters. The resulting Hamiltonian combines the on-site Cooper pairing with the off-site repulsion, and drives a continuous transition from the superfluid to the spin-density-wave phase. The coexistence region is reminiscent of a supersolid, yet the self-organized modulation appears in the spin density profile of a higher-spin representation, rather than in the number density profile. The proposal can be implemented with the existing techniques in ultracold atoms. Therefore it offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize cavity-induced multispin interactions in ultracold Fermi gases, leading to a superfluid to spin-density-wave phase transition.
motivation: Higher-spin systems can host new quantum phases, but controllable multispin interactions are challenging to achieve.
method: By engineering atom-cavity coupling via multiple Raman and cavity paths, effective interactions between pseudo-spin states are generated, with independent control over scattering channels.
result: The resulting Hamiltonian drives a continuous transition from superfluid to spin-density-wave phase, with a coexistence region reminiscent of supersolid but in spin density.
conclusion: The scheme offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics using existing ultracold atom techniques.

title: Asymptotically Exact Solution Of The non-Hermitian Disordered Interacting Hatano-Nelson Chain
authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, and Eduardo Miranda

This article presents an exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, equivalently formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain. The solution exhibits finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and shows that non-Hermiticity suppresses the entanglement entropy relative to the corresponding Hermitian model, eliminating the associated entanglement scaling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032012] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain exactly, finding divergent spin susceptibilities and suppressed entanglement entropy.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in low-dimensional systems, which may reveal novel thermodynamic and entanglement properties.
method: The authors use an asymptotically exact low-energy solution for a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, mapping it to a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain.
result: The solution shows finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and that non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy relative to the Hermitian model, eliminating entanglement scaling.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity fundamentally alters the entanglement structure and thermodynamic response of disordered interacting systems, with implications for understanding open quantum systems.

title: The Quantum Adiabatic Theorem For Non-Hermitian Dynamics
authors: G. M. V. S. Aponso, B. P. W. Fernando, K. K. W. A. S. Kumara, R. P. K. de Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative adiabatic estimate for a class of finite-dimensional non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger dynamics. The original non-Hermitian Hamiltonian is assumed to be diagonalizable with real spectrum and non-crossing eigenvalues. We then construct a dynamically compatible time-dependent metric operator, and its positive square root defines a Dyson map. The associated Dyson-transformed Hamiltonian is Hermitian. When this Dyson-transformed Hamiltonian satisfies the Hermitian adiabatic assumption, the standard resolvent-projection method gives an explicit adiabatic estimate in the Hermitian representation. Pulling this estimate back through the Dyson map gives an approximation in the original non-Hermitian representation. The resulting Dyson-pulled-back projections are then compared with the spectral projections of the original non-Hermitian Hamiltonian by using a contour-resolvent estimate. The final bound contains two contributions: the pulled-back Hermitian adiabatic error and the projection-comparison error. A two-level non-Hermitian model is presented to illustrate the hypotheses of the theorem and the two contributions appearing in the final estimate.
tldr: This paper proves a quantum adiabatic theorem for non-Hermitian dynamics with real spectra using a Dyson map to a Hermitian system.
motivation: Extend the quantum adiabatic theorem to non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant for open quantum systems and PT-symmetric quantum mechanics.
method: Construct a time-dependent metric operator and Dyson map to transform the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian into a Hermitian one, then apply standard Hermitian adiabatic estimates and pull back the result.
result: An explicit adiabatic error bound for non-Hermitian dynamics, consisting of a pulled-back Hermitian error and a projection-comparison error.
conclusion: The adiabatic approximation holds for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with real spectra under appropriate conditions, with a quantitative error estimate.

title: Band Engineering Of Exciton Polaritons In Resonant Polaritonic Metasurfaces
authors: Polina Pantiukhina, Daria Smirnova, Kirill Koshelev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polaritonic metasurfaces provide a versatile platform for engineering hybrid light-matter states through the interplay of optical resonances and excitonic excitations. Yet, predictive models often remain phenomenological and rely on coupled-mode equations. Here, we develop an effective Hamiltonian framework for exciton polaritons in resonant polaritonic metasurfaces, derived from a semiclassical single-pole description of excitonic polarization and a Green's-function description of guided-mode resonances. The resulting non-Hermitian Hamiltonian rigorously incorporates resonant photonic harmonics, multiple excitonic degrees of freedom, and radiative losses. The model reveals selection rules governing photonic-excitonic coupling classified by orbital multipole index and polarization, and shows that the minimal number of excitonic degrees of freedom equals the number of relevant photonic modes. We apply the framework to a bulk van der Waals WS[MATH] metasurface patterned into a hexagonal lattice of triangular holes and uncover a new geometry-controlled topological transition driven by dipole-quadrupole band inversion, distinct from the conventional breathing-honeycomb-lattice transition. Full-wave simulations confirm the predicted topological phase diagram and the emergence of photonic and polaritonic edge states at a topological interface. Our results establish a theoretical multimode framework for geometry-controlled bandstructure engineering in polaritonic metasurfaces, with applications in topological, chiral, and quantum integrated photonics.
tldr: This paper develops an effective Hamiltonian framework for exciton polaritons in resonant polaritonic metasurfaces, revealing a topological transition driven by dipole-quadrupole band inversion.
motivation: Predictive models for polaritonic metasurfaces often rely on phenomenological coupled-mode equations; a more rigorous theoretical framework is needed to engineer hybrid light-matter states.
method: The authors derive a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian from a semiclassical single-pole description of excitonic polarization and a Green's-function description of guided-mode resonances, incorporating resonant photonic harmonics, multiple excitonic degrees of freedom, and radiative losses.
result: The model reveals selection rules for photonic-excitonic coupling and predicts a geometry-controlled topological transition via dipole-quadrupole band inversion, confirmed by full-wave simulations showing photonic and polaritonic edge states.
conclusion: This work establishes a theoretical multimode framework for bandstructure engineering in polaritonic metasurfaces, with potential applications in topological, chiral, and quantum integrated photonics.

title: Baby Universes From Thermal Pure States In The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
authors: Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, And Alejandro Vilar López
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, and Alejandro Vilar López

We construct a simple two-dimensional holographic model of a closed “baby” universe. The baby universe spacetime originates from the black hole interior in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. The holographic description is a low-temperature thermal pure state of two Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The constr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a holographic model of a baby universe from thermal pure states in the SYK model, focusing on black hole interiors and Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity.
motivation: To understand the emergence of baby universes from black hole interiors using holographic duality.
method: The authors use the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model at low temperature to construct thermal pure states that holographically describe a baby universe spacetime in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity.
result: They show that a low-temperature thermal pure state of two SYK models corresponds to a closed baby universe originating from the black hole interior.
conclusion: The work provides a simple holographic realization of a baby universe, linking quantum gravity and condensed matter physics.

title: Simulating Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators With Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States
authors: Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, And Juraj Hasik
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, and Juraj Hasik

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPSs) provide a powerful variational framework for two-dimensional quantum matter and have been widely used to capture bosonic topological order, including chiral spin liquids. Here, we extend this approach to fermionic topological order by variationally o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046502] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) to simulate fermionic fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating a variational method for fermionic topological order.
motivation: Extending iPEPS to fermionic systems enables the study of fermionic topological phases, which are important for understanding fractional quantum Hall effects in lattice models.
method: The authors develop a fermionic iPEPS ansatz with Grassmann-valued tensors and apply it to the Haldane-Hubbard model at half-filling, using variational optimization to find ground states.
result: They obtain evidence for a fermionic fractional Chern insulator phase with Chern number 1/2, characterized by topological entanglement entropy and edge modes.
conclusion: Fermionic iPEPS provide a viable tool for simulating strongly correlated fermionic topological phases, opening avenues for studying fractional Chern insulators and related phenomena.

title: Transient Localization From Fractionalization: Vanishingly Small Energy Transport In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, and Michael Knap

Disorder-free localization is usually associated with dynamics far from equilibrium. Here, the authors uncover a new mechanism in the low-energy sector of clean, gapless quantum magnets: transient localization from mass-imbalanced fractionalization. Studying the dynamical response in the gapless phase of a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model, they show that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations in the ground state, preserving translation symmetry while strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034423] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient localization and suppressed energy transport in a clean, gapless quantum magnet due to fractionalization.
motivation: To understand how disorder-free localization can emerge in low-energy sectors of translation-invariant quantum magnets, and its effect on energy transport.
method: The authors analyze a Kitaev ladder model using analytical and numerical methods to study correlation spreading and energy transport in the gapless phase.
result: They find that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux disorder, preserving translation symmetry but strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a new example of disorder-free localization in a clean system, with implications for thermalization and transport in quantum magnets.

title: Probing non-Fermi-liquid Behavior Of A Composite Fermi Liquid Via Efficient Thermal Simulations
authors: Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, and Zi Yang Meng

The physics of two-dimensional electron gas in a perpendicular magnetic field, i.e., the quantum Hall system, is remarkably rich. At half filling of the lowest Landau level, it has been predicted that “composite fermions”—emergent quasiparticles consisting of an electron attached to two magnetic flu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065127] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses thermal simulations to study non-Fermi-liquid behavior in composite Fermi liquids at half-filled Landau levels.
motivation: Understanding the low-energy properties of composite fermions in quantum Hall systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors employ efficient thermal simulations, likely based on quantum Monte Carlo or tensor network methods, to compute thermodynamic quantities.
result: They observe signatures of non-Fermi-liquid behavior, such as deviations from Fermi liquid theory in specific heat or compressibility.
conclusion: The composite Fermi liquid exhibits non-Fermi-liquid behavior, providing insights into strongly correlated electron systems.

title: Symmetry-adapted Energy Estimation On Quantum Devices
authors: Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, and Ryotaro Arita

We present a symmetry-adapted extension of quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization that rigorously embeds space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware. The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model using both…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065124] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a symmetry-adapted quantum algorithm for energy estimation on quantum devices, benchmarked on the Hubbard model.
motivation: Quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices are limited by noise and qubit count; incorporating symmetries can reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors extend quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization to embed space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware.
result: The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model, demonstrating improved accuracy and reduced circuit depth compared to symmetry-agnostic approaches.
conclusion: Symmetry-adapted quantum algorithms can enhance the feasibility of quantum chemistry on near-term devices, but the work is primarily a computational chemistry application.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, focusing on fault-tolerant implementations.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring efficient embedding of circuits with long-range gates. The paper aims to reduce the overhead of SWAP gates in fault-tolerant settings.
method: The authors develop a heuristic algorithm that schedules SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints while minimizing circuit depth and gate count, considering the overhead of fault-tolerant error correction.
result: The proposed method reduces the number of SWAP gates and overall circuit depth compared to existing approaches, demonstrated on several benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The work provides practical compilation techniques for fault-tolerant quantum computing on near-term hardware, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and engineering-oriented rather than advancing fundamental quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:
Author(s): M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, and M. Eisenbach

Quantum embedding methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), provide a powerful framework for investigating strongly correlated materials. A central computational bottleneck in DMFT is in solving the Anderson impurity model (AIM), whose exact solution is classically intractable for large b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033066] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to solve the Anderson impurity model with particle-hole symmetry, targeting quantum embedding methods like DMFT.
motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is a computational bottleneck in DMFT for strongly correlated materials, and classical methods become intractable for large bath sizes.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that exploits particle-hole symmetry to reduce the number of qubits and gates, and implement it on a quantum simulator.
result: The quantum solver reproduces the exact solution for small systems and shows potential for scaling to larger systems where classical methods fail.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a proof-of-concept quantum solver for a condensed matter problem, but the approach is limited to particle-hole symmetric cases and does not provide new information-theoretic insights.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experiment.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity proofs only cover the dilute regime; this work extends the theoretical basis to match experimental conditions.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from permanent estimation and anticoncentration.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible complexity assumptions, and provide evidence for the robustness of the hardness.
conclusion: The results validate that current photonic experiments can achieve quantum advantage even in the saturated regime, strengthening the case for BosonSampling as a demonstration of quantum supremacy.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams with provable exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, as proven theoretically.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating the algorithm's scalability.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may offer a quantum advantage for certain instances.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural activity, bridging statistical physics and neuroscience.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from statistical physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for preparing arbitrary n-qubit quantum states and implementing diagonal unitaries, achieving Θ(4^n) scaling with ancilla.
motivation: Understanding the minimal number of T gates required for state preparation is crucial for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors improve prior work by Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, using techniques from quantum circuit synthesis and gate decomposition.
result: They show that the optimal T-count for approximating an arbitrary n-qubit state to error ε is Θ(4^n) when ancilla qubits are allowed, and similarly for diagonal unitaries.
conclusion: The work provides tight asymptotic bounds for T-count, with applications to parallel synthesis of tensor products of single-qubit unitaries.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks, with applications to NP and QMA.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks rely on commitments not known from standard assumptions; the authors aim to construct such protocols from LWE.
method: They extend the MPC-in-the-head technique to quantum computations, enabling zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA in the common reference string model.
result: Two three-round zero-knowledge arguments are presented: one for NP and one for QMA, both based on the learning with errors assumption.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper provides a near-optimal parameter tuning method for level-1 QAOA on Ising models, reducing the optimization to a structured signal-processing problem.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, even for shallow circuits. The authors aim to show that tuning angles for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured problem.
method: The authors prove that the QAOA1 expectation value is a partial Fourier series with frequencies determined by problem couplings, use Nyquist-Shannon to avoid aliasing, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm for global optimization.
result: They achieve polynomial-time global optimization with optimality certificate for commensurable weights, and prove that for regular graphs the optimal angle concentrates near zero, validating small-angle initialization.
conclusion: The method consistently outperforms coarsely optimized RQAOA and semidefinite programming on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits.

title: Decoder Comparability Across Quantum Software Stacks: Repeated-Round Surface And Digitized-GKP Syndrome Replay
authors: Dennis Delali Kwesi Wayo, Chinonso Onah, Rodrigo Alves Dias, Leonardo Goliatt, Zaher Mundher Yaseen Sven Groppe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a contract-preserving, family-aware comparison of decoder behavior across four syndrome-generation stacks (PennyLane, Qiskit, Cirq, and a LiDMaS+ reference) under a fixed replay interface. Request streams from repeated-round surface-code and digitized-GKP circuits are replayed through BP, MWPM, and UF with matched controls. The unified matrix spans 24 cells and achieves line-level integrity: [MATH] request lines, [MATH] response lines, response ratio [MATH] in every cell, zero parse failures, and zero decoder-name mismatches. Fifteen warning-no-syndrome events occur only in GKP-Cirq rows. Within-family ordering is stable in both families ([MATH]); source-averaged flip counts are 2.435, 4.768, and 5.870 for surface and 1.595, 2.908, and 3.681 for GKP. Relative to MWPM, BP reduces mean intervention volume by [MATH] in surface and [MATH] in GKP. Source-vs-reference effects are family dependent, with larger coherent shifts in GKP. Source-bootstrap ranks remain unchanged, and hidden-truth sidecars add an outer-code logical-parity error-rate check in which UF has the largest source-mean rate in both families. The comparison is stack-aware, contract-verified, and avoids raw cross-family threshold-equivalence claims.
tldr: This paper compares decoder behavior across different quantum software stacks for surface and GKP codes, focusing on syndrome replay and decoder performance metrics.
motivation: To evaluate and compare decoder implementations across multiple quantum software stacks to ensure consistency and identify stack-specific effects.
method: The authors replay syndrome data from repeated-round surface-code and digitized-GKP circuits through BP, MWPM, and UF decoders across four stacks (PennyLane, Qiskit, Cirq, LiDMaS+), using a unified matrix and contract verification.
result: The comparison reveals stable within-family ordering, family-dependent source-vs-reference effects, and that UF has the largest source-mean logical-parity error rate in both families.
conclusion: The study provides a stack-aware, contract-verified comparison of decoder behavior, but avoids raw cross-family threshold-equivalence claims.

title: Markov State Models Revisited: Principles And Algorithms For Unbiased Observables
authors: David Aristof, Robert J. Webber, Daniel M. Zuckerman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Markov state models (MSMs) have become ubiquitous tools for analyzing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations because of their simple, powerful premise: although complete MD sampling may be impossible, the MSM can "stitch together" transition probabilities derived from local sampling to provide a global picture of kinetics and mechanisms. In the standard MSM framework, the available MD data is organized into a single transition matrix, which is then used to estimate all observables at a lag time chosen so the coarse-grained dynamics are approximately Markovian. This approach leads to avoidable model bias and motivates long lag times that obscure short-timescale processes of interest. In contrast, this paper shows how to obtain unbiased coarse-grained observables at any fixed lag time and for any fixed coarse-graining in the limit of infinite, properly weighted data. The central idea is to replace the single-matrix framework with two transition matrices -- one representing equilibrium dynamics and another representing source-sink recycling dynamics -- and use the correct matrix or matrices to estimate the matched dynamical observables.
tldr: This paper presents a method to obtain unbiased coarse-grained observables from molecular dynamics simulations using two transition matrices instead of one.
motivation: Standard Markov state models introduce bias and require long lag times, obscuring short-timescale processes. The authors aim to eliminate this bias.
method: The authors replace the single transition matrix with two matrices: one for equilibrium dynamics and one for source-sink recycling dynamics, and use the appropriate matrix to estimate each observable.
result: In the limit of infinite, properly weighted data, the method yields unbiased coarse-grained observables at any fixed lag time and coarse-graining.
conclusion: The proposed two-matrix framework removes model bias inherent in standard MSMs, enabling accurate estimation of short-timescale dynamics.

title: Localization Transitions Of Diffusion Dynamics In Physical Networks
authors: Jun Yamamoto, Ivan Bonamassa, M\'arton P\'osfai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Network diffusion underlies many transport phenomena, with Laplacian modes setting how information spreads and relaxes. In physical networks, however, connectivity alone is not enough: node volumes introduce local dwell times that regulate how flow is stored before being propagated. Here we show that physical heterogeneity reshapes topology-driven localization, with the degree-volume ratio emerging as the relevant disorder parameter. We solve an analytical model in which ratio detuning qualitatively reorganizes the Laplacian spectrum, and demonstrate in empirical networks how degree-volume correlations shift extremal eigenmodes away from the nodes selected by topology alone. Our results reveal a general feature-rich-driven mechanism for localization control, showing that physicality non-trivially reshapes the disorder landscape governing network dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in diffusion dynamics on physical networks, focusing on the interplay between node volumes and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding how physical heterogeneity (node volumes) affects diffusion and localization in networks, beyond purely topological models.
method: Analytical model solving Laplacian spectrum with degree-volume ratio as disorder parameter, validated on empirical networks.
result: Degree-volume correlations shift extremal eigenmodes away from topology-selected nodes, revealing a feature-rich mechanism for localization control.
conclusion: Physicality non-trivially reshapes disorder landscape in network dynamics, offering new control over localization.

title: Tensor Network Machine Learning For Wildfire Susceptibility Mapping: From Grokking Dynamics To Quantum Mixedness Of Class Representations
authors: Domenico Pomarico, Alessandra Costantino, Gabriel Ramirez Sanchez, Loredana Bellantuono, Davide D' Al\`o, Mario Elia, Alessandro Fania, Francesco Giordano, Niloofar Kheirkhahan, Raffaele Lafortezza, Ester Pantaleo, Sabina Tangaro, Roberto Bellotti, Alfonso Monaco, Nicola Amoroso
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum-inspired tensor network framework for wildfire susceptibility classification in the Gargano region is introduced, leveraging AlphaEarth embeddings and Matrix Product State models. The approach combines scalable geospatial representations with an interpretable quantum mask, enabling both binary and multiclass classification of wildfire susceptibility. Beyond predictive performance, the study reveals a pronounced grokking transition in the binary case and provides a detailed analysis of inter-class confusion in the multiclass setting. By introducing level-resolved mixedness diagnostics based on reduced density matrices, we show that the MPS classifier naturally encodes a hierarchy of class distinguishability, with non-adjacent categories becoming more separable than neighboring ones. These results demonstrate that tensor network models not only achieve competitive classification accuracy but also offer a physically grounded framework to quantify and interpret class separability in complex environmental datasets.
tldr: This paper applies tensor network machine learning to wildfire susceptibility mapping, with no direct connection to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to improve wildfire susceptibility classification using quantum-inspired tensor networks, but the application is purely environmental and lacks quantum information or thermodynamics content.
method: They use AlphaEarth embeddings and Matrix Product State models for binary and multiclass classification, and introduce level-resolved mixedness diagnostics based on reduced density matrices.
result: The model shows a grokking transition in binary classification and reveals a hierarchy of class distinguishability in multiclass settings.
conclusion: Tensor network models can achieve competitive accuracy and provide interpretable class separability, but the work is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Enantioselective Optical Trapping And Characterization Of All Dielectric Disorder-enabled Chiral Particles
authors: Guilherme T. Moura, Tanja Schoger, Kain\~a G. Diniz, Marcel A. B. Morte, Diney S. Ether Jr, Leonardo de S. Menezes, Yicui Kang, Emiliano Cort\'es, Cyriaque Genet, Nathan B. Viana, Felipe A. Pinheiro, Paulo A. Maia Neto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We trap submicroscopic silica spheres coated with randomly distributed titanium dioxide nanoparticles in optical tweezers with Laguerre-Gaussian modes and observe orbital dynamics that differ from those of achiral silica spheres. We show that the disordered nanoparticle coating generates an effective chiral geometry, giving rise to enhanced enantioselective chiral optical forces and a measurable modification of the orbital period. A theoretical model based on the Mie-Debye formalism, including optical aberrations, not only quantitatively explains the experimental results but also allows to characterize the Pasteur parameter quantifying the chiroptical response of individual composite particles. These findings constitute direct experimental evidence of chiral optical forces exerted by structured light beams on individual chiral particles and identify disorder-enabled, all-dielectric particles as a versatile material platform to tailor chiral optical forces at the nanoscale.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enantioselective optical trapping of chiral particles using Laguerre-Gaussian beams, with a focus on optical forces and chiroptical response.
motivation: To provide direct experimental evidence of chiral optical forces on individual particles and to develop a versatile platform for nanoscale chiral manipulation.
method: Silica spheres coated with TiO2 nanoparticles are trapped in optical tweezers with Laguerre-Gaussian modes; orbital dynamics are observed and modeled using Mie-Debye formalism with optical aberrations.
result: The disordered coating creates effective chirality, leading to enhanced enantioselective forces and measurable changes in orbital period; the model quantifies the Pasteur parameter.
conclusion: Disorder-enabled all-dielectric particles are a promising platform for tailoring chiral optical forces at the nanoscale.

title: Quantum Gravity Simulation: Quantum Simulation With A Minimum Length Based On The Generalised Uncertainty Principle
authors: Jack Keable-Elliott, David J. Bacon, Andrew Burbanks, Jaewoo Joo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a recipe for simulating one-dimensional quantum systems for low and high energies with [MATH] qubits within the framework of first quantisation. Assuming a minimum grid spacing [MATH] in the finite-difference method, the generalised uncertainty principle (GUP) is derived analytically and shows distinct properties for low- and high-energy quantum systems. In the low-energy regime, the GUP approaches to the standard Heisenberg uncertainty principle (HUP) for [MATH]. However, for finite [MATH], the GUP mathematically provides three different regions dependent on the average momentum and suggests that a wavefunction can exhibit a single-point localisation at the finite momentum uncertainty due to lack of grid resolution. We then derive a new expression for the high-energy momentum and focus on two specific cases relevant to relativistic aspects. First, if the HUP is relaxed and the high-energy momentum is matched to the special-relativistic one, the resulting GUP predicts the existence of a minimum length with non-zero mass for high energy despite the continuous limit [MATH]. Second, enforcing consistency with the HUP allows the recovery of a canonical high-energy representation with no minimum length. But this requirement brings incompatibility with the special-relativistic momentum and suggests a modified energy-momentum equation. Therefore, we believe that the proposed momentum formulation provides a novel pathway to investigate quantum gravity phenomena for high energy using quantum simulation tools.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum simulation recipe for one-dimensional systems with a minimum length derived from the generalized uncertainty principle, aiming to simulate quantum gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum gravity effects using quantum simulation tools by incorporating a minimum length scale into the simulation framework.
method: The authors use a finite-difference method with a minimum grid spacing to derive the generalized uncertainty principle analytically, and then formulate a high-energy momentum expression for simulation.
result: The GUP shows three regions depending on average momentum, and for high energy, a minimum length can exist with non-zero mass, or consistency with HUP leads to a modified energy-momentum equation.
conclusion: The proposed momentum formulation provides a novel pathway to investigate quantum gravity phenomena using quantum simulation, but the connection to the user's research directions is weak.

title: On Solutions Of The Killingbeck Potential And Clarifying Comments On A Related Analytical Approach
authors: Fatma Zohra Khaled, Mustafa Moumni, Mokhtar Falek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The work presents analytical solutions to the Schrodinger equation for the Killingbeck potential, a Hybrid model combining harmonic, linear and Coulomb terms, and which is also an approximate model of Yukawa-type potentials. The radial Schrodinger equation is solved by means of the series expansion method, thus yielding the exact expressions of both bound-states solutions and eigen-functions for the systems; these systems include quarkonium and confined hydrogen-like atoms in plasma environments. Furthermore, we offer a constructive commentary on the work of Obu et al. (East Eur. J. Phys. 3, 146-157, 2023), with the aim of clarifying a mathematical misstatement used in their analytical treatment of analogous systems.
tldr: This paper solves the Schrödinger equation for the Killingbeck potential using series expansion, providing analytical bound-state solutions and eigenfunctions for quarkonium and confined hydrogen-like atoms.
motivation: To obtain exact analytical solutions for the Killingbeck potential, which models quarkonium and atoms in plasma, and to correct a mathematical error in a previous work.
method: The radial Schrödinger equation is solved via series expansion method, yielding exact expressions for bound-state energies and wavefunctions.
result: Exact analytical solutions for the Killingbeck potential are derived, and a mathematical misstatement in Obu et al. (2023) is clarified.
conclusion: The work provides correct analytical solutions for a hybrid potential and highlights the importance of rigorous mathematical treatment in quantum mechanical problems.

title: Weakly Nonlinear Dynamics Of Unstable Modes In Jammed Amorphous Solids
authors: Kota Noto, Harukuni Ikeda, Kuniyasu Saitoh, Hisao Hayakawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural evolution in jammed amorphous solids by analyzing the eigenmodes of a generalized Hessian matrix that incorporates spatial modulation via wave numbers. Unlike the conventional Hessian, this generalized formulation captures linearly unstable modes through a Fourier-based extension of the Hessian matrix, enabling us to study responses beyond the mechanically stable regime. We demonstrate that the excitation of unstable eigenmodes leads to structural rearrangements independent of the initial perturbation by the simulation. Furthermore, we derive a weakly nonlinear amplitude equation to describe the growth and saturation of these unstable modes, analogous to the Landau equation. Our framework provides a pathway to understand instability-driven configuration changes in disordered solids.
tldr: This paper studies weakly nonlinear dynamics of unstable modes in jammed amorphous solids using a generalized Hessian matrix.
motivation: Understanding structural evolution in disordered solids beyond the mechanically stable regime is important for materials science.
method: The authors analyze eigenmodes of a generalized Hessian matrix with spatial modulation and derive a weakly nonlinear amplitude equation analogous to the Landau equation.
result: Excitation of unstable eigenmodes leads to structural rearrangements independent of initial perturbation, and the amplitude equation describes growth and saturation.
conclusion: The framework provides a pathway to understand instability-driven configuration changes in disordered solids.

title: Super-Resonance: Interference-Driven Suppression Of Radiative Decay Across Wave Physics
authors: Igor V. Minin, Oleg V. Minin, Ilia L. Rasskazov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-resonance has been coined independently for collective modes of acoustic cavity arrays (Tolstoy), extreme high-[MATH] states of dielectric resonators in photonics, and magnon-polaron bound states in magnonics, and is now applied interchangeably to physically distinct phenomena. We organise this review around the one usage admitting a precise, field-agnostic definition: a mode whose radiative linewidth is driven toward zero by destructive interference among its radiation channels, [MATH], while the bare single-channel coupling remains large. The canonical realisation is the Friedrich-Wintgen scenario of two modes sharing a continuum. The same non-Hermitian eigenvalue structure recurs in Tolstoy's acoustic arrays, photonic bound states in the continuum and quasi-BIC supercavity modes, anapoles, dark modes of coherent perfect absorbers, parity-time-symmetric devices near exceptional points, magnonic dark modes, and topological edge modes. We survey these realisations field by field and distil transferable design rules and figures of merit. We then disambiguate super-resonance from two families sharing the "super-" prefix: coherent enhancement, in which coupling to the continuum is collectively increased rather than suppressed (Dicke super-radiance, superscattering, whispering-gallery modes); and integer-commensurability locking (mean-motion, wave-particle, and Floquet resonances). Amplification, as in black-hole super-radiance, is likewise distinguished.
tldr: A review of super-resonance phenomena across wave physics, focusing on interference-driven suppression of radiative decay.
motivation: To disambiguate the term 'super-resonance' and unify diverse physical realizations under a common non-Hermitian eigenvalue framework.
method: Survey of acoustic, photonic, magnonic, and topological systems exhibiting Friedrich-Wintgen-type interference, with comparative analysis of design rules and figures of merit.
result: Identifies the Friedrich-Wintgen scenario as the canonical mechanism and distinguishes super-resonance from coherent enhancement and commensurability locking.
conclusion: Super-resonance is a universal wave phenomenon with transferable design principles across fields, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Propagation Dynamics Of High-gain Vortex Beams In Symmetry-broken Media Via Forward And Backward Three-wave Mixing
authors: Fan Meng, Hao Zhu, Xin-Yao Huang, Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, vortex light, a distinctive form of structured light, has attracted considerable attention owing to its unique properties and the rich physical phenomena arising from its interaction with matter. In this paper, we investigate the propagation dynamics of vortex beams in a symmetry-broken three-level system based on forward and backward three-wave mixing (TWM) processes. We find that both processes enable the transfer of high-gain vortex light, with the associated topological charges obeying identical algebraic relations. The forward process exhibits periodic oscillatory transmission and modulates the transverse spatial profile of the generated signal vortex field, whereas the backward process features stable transmission and produces a signal field with higher gain and improved fidelity. Under the Autler-Townes splitting (ATS) regime, the probe field detuning in both schemes has a negligible influence on the gain. Optical depth influences only the rate at which the gain approaches its maximum, while the peak value remains unchanged. These results constitute a meaningful extension of the work reported in reference [40] and may provide a feasible approach for quantum communication, quantum computation, and the generation of high-gain, high-fidelity vortex light.
tldr: This paper studies the propagation dynamics of vortex beams in symmetry-broken media via three-wave mixing, focusing on gain and fidelity of vortex light transfer.
motivation: Vortex beams have unique properties useful for quantum communication and computation, but their propagation in nonlinear media is not fully understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze forward and backward three-wave mixing processes in a symmetry-broken three-level system, deriving equations for the signal field and examining gain and spatial profile.
result: Both processes transfer topological charge with identical algebraic relations; forward process yields oscillatory transmission while backward process provides stable, higher gain and fidelity.
conclusion: The results extend previous work and suggest a feasible approach for generating high-gain, high-fidelity vortex light for quantum applications.

title: Dirac-vortex Modes Beyond The Continuum Limit
authors: Jiayu Fan, Jiusi Yu, Aoning Luo, Yiyi Yao, Shijie Kang, Xiexuan Zhang, Haitao Li, Biye Xie, Xiao-Dong Chen, Xiaoxiao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dirac-vortex modes (DVMs) in Kekule-modulated lattices provide a topological route to wave confinement and are commonly described by the continuum Jackiw-Rossi model, in which the initial phase acts as a redundant gauge degree of freedom and does not affect observables of the mode. Here we show that this picture breaks down in discrete lattices when the complex mass texture that induces the DVMs no longer satisfies the slowly varying envelope approximation. In this regime, lattice discreteness turns the initial phase into a physically observable parameter that shifts the DVM center. By further introducing a sublattice-antisymmetric perturbation, we convert this phase-dependent center motion into a continuous spectral response of the DVM, enabling its frequency tuning across nearly the entire topological bandgap. Our simulation and experimental results agree well with a revised continuum model accounting for the mode-center motion. Within this perturbative framework, the model shows that the frequency shift exhibits a sinusoidal-like dependence on the initial phase. These findings reveal initial phase-sensitivity of the DVMs realized in lattices, an important and basic feature absent from the ideal continuum Jackiw-Rossi model, and demonstrate initial phase engineering as a potential pathway towards reconfigurable photonic devices.
tldr: This paper studies Dirac-vortex modes in discrete photonic lattices, revealing that the initial phase becomes observable and can tune the mode frequency.
motivation: The continuum Jackiw-Rossi model predicts that the initial phase is a redundant gauge degree of freedom, but this assumption breaks down in discrete lattices, motivating a study of phase effects.
method: The authors use simulation and experiments on Kekule-modulated photonic lattices, comparing with a revised continuum model that accounts for mode-center motion.
