result: They find that lattice discreteness makes the initial phase physically observable, shifting the mode center, and that a sublattice-antisymmetric perturbation converts this motion into a continuous spectral response.
conclusion: The work demonstrates initial phase engineering as a pathway for reconfigurable photonic devices, highlighting a feature absent in the continuum model.

title: Motility Destabilizes An Absorbing-state Flock
authors: Narayan Dutt Sharma, Subroto Mukerjee, Chandan Dasgupta, Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activity, when it takes the form of motility, is generally seen to promote order in many-body systems. Here we present a one-dimensional lattice model that, in the non-motile limit, exhibits absorbing ferromagnetic states. When activity is introduced through biased motility, these absorbing state are destabilised and the system instead undergoes a transition from an ordered flock to a disordered state as the alignment strength is decreased. A finite-size scaling analysis of physical quantities reveals a continuous transition with critical exponents satisfying the hyperscaling relation in one dimension, providing quantitative evidence for the activity-induced disorder.
tldr: A one-dimensional lattice model shows that motility destabilizes absorbing ferromagnetic states, leading to a continuous order-disorder transition.
motivation: To understand how activity (motility) affects ordering in many-body systems, contrary to the common belief that activity promotes order.
method: A one-dimensional lattice model with biased motility and alignment interactions is studied via finite-size scaling analysis.
result: Motility destabilizes absorbing ferromagnetic states, causing a continuous transition from ordered flock to disordered state with critical exponents satisfying hyperscaling in 1D.
conclusion: Activity-induced disorder is demonstrated, providing quantitative evidence that motility can suppress order in certain systems.

title: Slack-Free Deep-Unfolded Combinatorial Optimization Solver For Inequality Constraints
authors: Ryo Hagiwara, Shunta Arai, Satoshi Takabe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) is used to solve combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). When COPs are implemented on quantum annealers, they are typically encoded as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems, but constraint encodings often increase the number of qubits and the embedding overhead. This issue is particularly important for COPs with inequality constraints, where standard slack-variable formulations introduce additional binary variables. Unbalanced penalization (UP) avoids slack variables, but the original UP formulation requires tuning two penalty coefficients and contains a squared residual term that can increase the number of quadratic couplings. In this paper, we propose the unbalanced penalization Ohzeki method (UPOM), which combines UP with the Ohzeki method for inequality-constrained COPs. UPOM replaces the two static penalty coefficients of original UP with an auxiliary-variable update and removes the squared residual term from the Hamiltonian used for sampling. We further propose the deep-unfolded unbalanced penalization Ohzeki method (DU-UPOM), which learns the step-size schedule of the UPOM update from training instances. Numerical experiments on random knapsack problems show that UPOM improves over original UP and that DU-UPOM reaches optimal solutions in fewer iterations than fixed-step UPOM and other baseline. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces the tuning and embedding burdens of UP while making the Ohzeki method trainable for inequality constraints.
tldr: This paper proposes a slack-free method for solving inequality-constrained combinatorial optimization problems on quantum annealers by combining unbalanced penalization with the Ohzeki method and deep unfolding.
motivation: Standard QUBO encodings of inequality constraints introduce slack variables that increase qubit count and embedding overhead, while existing slack-free methods require manual tuning of penalty coefficients.
method: The authors propose UPOM, which replaces static penalty coefficients with an auxiliary-variable update and removes the squared residual term, and DU-UPOM, which learns the step-size schedule via deep unfolding.
result: Numerical experiments on random knapsack problems show that UPOM outperforms original UP, and DU-UPOM reaches optimal solutions in fewer iterations than fixed-step UPOM and baselines.
conclusion: The proposed framework reduces tuning and embedding burdens for inequality constraints in quantum annealing, making the Ohzeki method trainable for such problems.

title: On Unconventional Discretisations
authors: Basil Grammaticos, Thamizharasi Tamizhmani, Ralph Willox
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present various discretisation techniques that mark a departure from the classical algorithms of numerical analysis, in the aim of preserving the physical behaviour of the solutions to the differential systems we are discretising, even for discretisation steps that are not very small. These techniques are inspired by the principles laid down by Mickens and are close to those proposed by Hirota and Kahan. Detailed applications of these methods are presented for the logistic equation and for the Lotka-Volterra system. We discuss the importance of preserving positivity whenever the latter is an expected property of the solution and give a practical rule for achieving this. Possible problems arising from the discretisations we propose are also discussed. A section is devoted to discretisations of integrable systems aimed at preserving integrability. Finally we conclude this review with a discussion of the possible relevance of a discrete space-time.
tldr: This paper reviews unconventional discretization techniques for differential equations, focusing on preserving physical behavior and integrability, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To present discretization methods that preserve physical properties of differential equations even for large step sizes, departing from classical numerical analysis.
method: The paper reviews techniques inspired by Mickens, Hirota, and Kahan, applying them to the logistic equation and Lotka-Volterra system, and discusses positivity preservation and integrability.
result: The methods successfully preserve positivity and integrability in the examples, but the paper is a review without novel results.
conclusion: Unconventional discretizations can be useful for preserving physical behavior, but the relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Mc-bridge: A Modular Receiver-Chain Simulation Framework For OECT-Based Molecular Communication
authors: Ozgur B. Akan Hongbin Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic electrochemical transistor (OECT)-based molecular communication (MC) receivers connect transport and binding to device current, noise, calibration, and detection. We present MC-BRIDGE (Molecular Communication Bioelectronic Receiver-chain Integrated Design and Guided Evaluation), a modular framework linking release, extracellular diffusion, finite-area observation, stochastic binding, and OECT transduction to charge-domain detection. On an independent electrical time grid, it generates sequence-wide multichannel colored noise, performs control-channel referencing and charge integration, and supports molecule-shift-keying (MoSK), concentration-shift-keying (CSK), and Hybrid decisions. Through common module interfaces, it estimates symbol error rate (SER) and decoded-symbol mutual information and analyzes inter-symbol interference (ISI). At nominal separation, the passive finite-area observer retains 27.5 percent of the center-point decision-charge magnitude, while correlation between the selective and control channels determines whether control referencing helps. After adaptive search, held-out records with seeds disjoint from search and calibration test the selected and next-lower budgets, yielding a tested-grid upper bound on the minimum budget meeting the SER target. This passive-field test resets receptor occupancy, excludes ISI, and calibrates thresholds on separate records at each operating point. Retaining transport and receptor memory instead produces high SER. Thus, geometry, covariance, calibration, and memory can change receiver conclusions.
tldr: This paper presents a simulation framework for OECT-based molecular communication receivers, focusing on modeling transport, binding, and detection in biological environments.
motivation: Molecular communication is a bio-inspired paradigm, but this work is heavily focused on engineering aspects of OECT-based receivers rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The framework models release, diffusion, binding, and OECT transduction, generating colored noise and supporting various modulation schemes to estimate symbol error rate and mutual information.
result: At nominal separation, the passive observer retains 27.5% of center-point decision-charge magnitude; control referencing effectiveness depends on channel correlation; memory effects increase SER.
conclusion: Geometry, covariance, calibration, and memory significantly affect receiver performance, highlighting the need for careful modeling in molecular communication.

title: Equilibrium Causal Games: Separation, Identification, And The Identifiability Of Cyclic Latent States
authors: Neda Nazemi Faraz Dadgostari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power grids, markets, and interacting populations, settle into feedback driven equilibria observed through unknown sensors. Our Equilibrium Causal Game (ECG) joins a game to its cyclic causal model, hidden inputs, sensor map, and rules for interventions and equilibrium selection; interventions edit declared objects and recompute equilibrium. Under stated conditions, ECG-separation is sound but incomplete in our examples. Back-door/half-trek routes identify observed queries. Yet for an untouched rotationally symmetric Gaussian block, second moments determine only a source-frame rotation, across which distinct-variable effects generically change. Unknown sensing creates a separate ambiguity. In passive stable linear models without self-effects, unknown wiring and full-rank unknown sensing leave [MATH] completely unidentified for [MATH]. Under LiNG, non-Gaussianity removes the source rotation; mechanism interventions separate sensing from interactions. With unknown support, invariant sensing, aligned responses, and well-posed single-target interventions identify [MATH] up to declared equivalence. Of [MATH] targets, [MATH] suffice exactly when the sole untargeted node directly parents all others; otherwise [MATH] are needed. Acquisition probes are excluded; known wiring gives no universal count. With nonlinear sensing, isotropic Gaussian source blocks admit hidden twists within and across blocks in labelled environments preserving required radial laws. Conversely, under stated positivity, informative one-block changes, rank, and irreducibility conditions, the finest independent source-block representation is identified within the stated alternative class up to block permutation and blockwise coordinate changes, but not downstream mechanisms or the sensor/interaction split. Together, these results show which causal conclusions equilibrium data support and which require targeted experiments.
tldr: This paper introduces Equilibrium Causal Games (ECG) to model feedback-driven equilibria in systems like power grids and markets, focusing on causal identification from equilibrium data.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in systems that settle into equilibrium is challenging due to feedback loops and unknown sensors; the paper aims to provide a framework for identifying causal structures from such data.
method: The authors define ECG as a combination of a game with a cyclic causal model, hidden inputs, and sensor maps, and analyze conditions for separation and identification using back-door and half-trek criteria, as well as non-Gaussianity and intervention strategies.
result: They show that under certain conditions, ECG-separation is sound but incomplete; second moments determine only a source-frame rotation in symmetric Gaussian blocks, and unknown wiring and sensing leave parameters unidentified unless specific interventions or non-Gaussianity are used.
conclusion: The results delineate which causal conclusions can be drawn from equilibrium data and which require targeted experiments, highlighting fundamental identifiability limits.

title: Extinction Depth And Q-ary Error-Correcting Codes For The Limited Permutation Channel
authors: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy Noam Ben Shimon (yohananov)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the radius-one limited permutation channel, errors consist of disjoint adjacent transpositions. A correcting code must separate distinct codewords: their error balls may not contain a common received word. Hamming distance does not ensure this, because disjoint swaps can make words differing in many positions confusable. For block-concatenation codes, earlier work tested each possible collision only through the longer initial block. This sufficient condition is not necessary: we exhibit a valid ternary block set that it does not certify. We introduce extinction depth, which tracks unresolved first-block pairs through later block extensions, and prove that their extinction at one common finite horizon certifies correction at every length. The criterion gives explicit [MATH] and [MATH] block sets with rates above [MATH] and [MATH]. No block-set-independent depth bound exists: we give an exact linear family, verify a quadratic formula for every [MATH], and derive a polynomial-time finite-graph test. For growing alphabets, the normalized correction loss lies between [MATH] and [MATH], while explicit finite-length covers improve finite-alphabet upper bounds. We develop a parallel directed-extinction theory for detection, including an all-length block criterion, a set unresolved by the earlier test, and exact corridor depth [MATH]. Stable type lifting yields optimal first-order loss [MATH], and weak-zigzag codes improve the [MATH] lower bounds. Finally, window restriction, cancellation, and a bounded pending-input frontier extend the criterion and its finite-state verification to every fixed displacement radius [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies error-correcting codes for the limited permutation channel, focusing on extinction depth and block-concatenation codes.
motivation: The limited permutation channel models errors as adjacent transpositions, and existing Hamming distance-based criteria are insufficient for ensuring correctability.
method: The authors introduce the concept of extinction depth to track unresolved first-block pairs through block extensions, and develop finite-graph tests and parallel directed-extinction theory.
result: They provide explicit block sets with rates above certain thresholds, derive bounds on normalized correction loss, and extend the criterion to arbitrary displacement radii.
conclusion: The work advances coding theory for permutation channels but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Break-Resilient Codes
authors: Canran Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Break-resilient codes protect a word against an omniscient adversary who breaks it at arbitrary boundaries between adjacent symbols. For binary codewords of length~[MATH] subject to at most~[MATH] breaks, the best known explicit construction for this model has redundancy~[MATH], whereas the information-theoretic lower bound is~[MATH]. In this paper, we close this gap by presenting a break-resilient code with redundancy~[MATH] when~[MATH] for a fixed [MATH], matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to a constant factor. The key idea is to compute a short algebraic fingerprint of the message, which enables the decoder to reject incorrect assemblies of the received fragments.
tldr: This paper presents optimal break-resilient codes that protect binary words against an adversary who breaks them at arbitrary boundaries, achieving redundancy matching the information-theoretic lower bound.
motivation: Break-resilient codes are needed to protect data integrity when an adversary can break a codeword into fragments at unknown positions. The gap between known constructions and the lower bound needed to be closed.
method: The authors compute a short algebraic fingerprint of the message, enabling the decoder to reject incorrect assemblies of received fragments, and use this to construct codes with optimal redundancy.
result: The proposed code achieves redundancy O(k log n) when k = O(n^{1-ε}) for a fixed ε>0, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to a constant factor.
conclusion: The work closes the gap between upper and lower bounds for break-resilient codes, providing an explicit construction that is optimal in redundancy.

title: Investigation Of Steep For Secure Communications Over Simo And Miso Channels Subject To Full-Duplex Jamming And Eavesdropping
authors: Yingbo Hua Md Saydur Rahman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure communications over SIMO and MISO channels between wireless nodes are commonly encountered in applications and widely considered in the literature. This paper investigates such a problem by considering a newly proposed scheme called secrecy-message transmission by echoing encrypted probes (STEEP). We focus on a type of heavily eavesdropped channels where an aggressive eavesdropper (Eve) has multiple antennas and is capable of jamming and eavesdropping in the full-duplex mode. Assuming optimal jamming and eavesdropping by Eve, we present the secrecy rates achievable by STEEP in two forms: using SIMO channel in phase 1 and using MISO channel in phase 2, and vice versa. With any given channel condition between every pair of nodes and any finite jamming power by Eve, the secrecy rate of STEEP in either form is shown to be positive subject to a positive power in phase 1 and a sufficiently large power in phase 2. The connections between STEEP in either form and the conventional SIMO and MISO schemes are provided, and their secrecy rates are compared comprehensively subject to random fading channels and finite transmit powers.
tldr: This paper proposes a secure communication scheme (STEEP) for SIMO/MISO channels under full-duplex jamming and eavesdropping, focusing on classical wireless security.
motivation: To achieve positive secrecy rates in heavily eavesdropped wireless channels where an adversary can jam and eavesdrop simultaneously.
method: The STEEP scheme uses encrypted probes in two phases (SIMO and MISO) and analyzes achievable secrecy rates under optimal jamming by Eve.
result: STEEP achieves positive secrecy rates for any finite jamming power given sufficient power in phase 2, and comparisons with conventional schemes are provided.
conclusion: STEEP is effective for secure communications in adversarial SIMO/MISO channels, but the work is purely classical and does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimization Of Mimo Steep For Secure Communications Over Mimome Channels
authors: Yingbo Hua Dinglin Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A transmission scheme for secure communications, called secret-message transmission by echoing encrypted probes (STEEP), can deliver a positive secrecy rate, even when eavesdropping channels are much stronger than that between users, subject to sufficient asymmetric power allocations from users. This paper considers an optimization problem for STEEP applied to MIMO (or MIMOME) channels between multi-antenna users and multi-antenna Eve. We reveal for the first time a significant increase of the achievable secrecy rate of MIMO STEEP using optimized precoders.
tldr: This paper optimizes precoders for a MIMO STEEP secure communication scheme over MIMOME channels to increase achievable secrecy rate.
motivation: Secure communication over MIMO channels is important, and STEEP can achieve positive secrecy rate even when eavesdropping channels are strong. Optimizing precoders can further improve performance.
method: The authors formulate an optimization problem for precoder design in MIMO STEEP and derive solutions to maximize achievable secrecy rate.
result: They reveal a significant increase in achievable secrecy rate using optimized precoders compared to non-optimized ones.
conclusion: Optimized precoders greatly enhance the secrecy performance of MIMO STEEP, making it more effective for secure communications.

title: Harnessing Heterogeneous Data For Conditional Optimization Via Optimal Transport
authors: Qinyu Wu Jonathan Yu-Meng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conditional optimization tailors decisions to contextual or event information, but its practical use is often limited by the difficulty of learning the relevant conditional distribution from finite samples of a target joint distribution. This challenge is especially acute when target joint data are scarce or unavailable, or when few observations fall in the conditioning region of interest. Related joint data may be available from multiple sources, such as different stores, markets, populations, or operating environments, but these sources may be biased relative to the target distribution and cannot be pooled naively. We develop a distributionally robust framework based on optimal transport (OT) for harnessing such heterogeneous data in conditional optimization. The framework constructs ambiguity sets over joint distributions using OT distances to empirical source distributions and optimizes worst-case conditional performance over plausible target laws. We propose three OT ambiguity sets that capture different ways of using heterogeneous sources: enforcing simultaneous source consistency, aggregating source discrepancies through weights, and centering the ambiguity set at an OT barycenter. We derive tractable reformulations, establish feasibility conditions, discuss parameter choices, and characterize the relationships among the formulations, revealing trade-offs between robustness, information aggregation, and computational complexity. We demonstrate the value of the framework through a conditional assortment problem using demand and product-feature data from multiple stores.
tldr: This paper develops a distributionally robust framework using optimal transport for conditional optimization with heterogeneous data sources.
motivation: Conditional optimization often suffers from scarce target joint data; heterogeneous related sources exist but are biased and cannot be pooled naively.
method: The framework constructs ambiguity sets over joint distributions using OT distances to empirical source distributions and optimizes worst-case conditional performance.
result: Three OT ambiguity sets are proposed with tractable reformulations, feasibility conditions, and trade-offs between robustness, information aggregation, and complexity.
conclusion: The framework effectively harnesses heterogeneous data for conditional optimization, demonstrated on a conditional assortment problem.

title: The Missing Two-point Inequality In Weissler's Conjecture
authors: Paata Ivanisvili Yi C. Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weissler's conjectured characterization of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube remained open in the ranges [MATH] and [MATH]. Ivanisvili--Nazarov established the diagonal cases. We prove the remaining strict off-diagonal cases through the corresponding two-point inequality. In fact, our argument proves the two-point inequality for every [MATH] and, by duality, for every [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves the remaining off-diagonal cases of Weissler's conjecture on complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.
motivation: Weissler's conjecture on complex hypercontractivity had open ranges; the diagonal cases were known, but off-diagonal cases remained unproven.
method: The authors prove the two-point inequality for all parameters using duality arguments.
result: They establish the strict off-diagonal cases, completing the characterization of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.
conclusion: The conjecture is now fully resolved, providing a complete description of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.

title: Rational Spectra For Finite Hadamard Pairs And Bounded Spectral Sets On The Real Line
authors: Zi-Jian Song Xiao-Ye Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite spectral pair \((A,\Gamma)\) with \(A\subset\mathbb Z\), \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), and \(0\in\Gamma\) has a rational spectrum, that is, \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). Our argument relies on a modulus rigidity theorem for generalizedVandermonde systems satisfying inverse-orthogonality relations, constructed by hyperbolic positive-definite kernels. Combined with Galois conjugation and Kronecker's theorem, this rigidity forces the associated exponential nodes to be roots of unity. As an application, using the periodicity and fiberization of one-dimensional spectra, we show that every spectrum \(\Lambda\) of a bounded measurable spectral set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R\) with \(|\Omega|=1\) and \(0\in\Lambda\) is contained in \(\mathbb Q\). This rational-spectrum result completes a chain of equivalences proven by Dutkay and Lai, which reduces the full one-dimensional Fuglede's conjecture to its finite cyclic analogues over \(_n\).
tldr: This paper proves that finite spectral pairs with integer first component have rational spectra, and applies this to show that spectra of bounded measurable spectral sets on the real line are rational, contributing to Fuglede's conjecture.
motivation: To resolve the one-dimensional Fuglede conjecture by establishing that spectral sets must have rational spectra, reducing the problem to finite cyclic groups.
method: Uses a modulus rigidity theorem for generalized Vandermonde systems with inverse-orthogonality relations, combined with Galois conjugation and Kronecker's theorem.
result: Every finite spectral pair (A,Γ) with A⊂ℤ, Γ⊂ℝ/ℤ, 0∈Γ has Γ⊂ℚ/ℤ; every spectrum Λ of a bounded measurable spectral set Ω⊂ℝ with |Ω|=1 and 0∈Λ is contained in ℚ.
conclusion: The rational spectrum result completes a chain of equivalences that reduces the full one-dimensional Fuglede conjecture to its finite cyclic analogues.

title: Duality And Reverse Self-Dual Constructions For Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Hongchang Li, Zhihao Zhu, Weijun Fang, Jun Zhang, Sihuang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon (HRS) codes form a class of maximum-distance-separable codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman metric and may be viewed as a derivative-evaluation extension of classical Reed-Solomon codes. For generalized Reed-Solomon codes, the Euclidean dual is again a generalized Reed-Solomon code. In this paper, we investigate the corresponding duality problem for HRS codes. Using a residue-theoretic argument, we derive an explicit component-wise representation for the Euclidean dual of an HRS code. The formula shows that, in general, the Euclidean dual is not an HRS code. Instead, it is blockwise upper-triangularly equivalent to a reverse-order HRS evaluation code, where the reversal occurs in the hyperderivative orders within each evaluation block. In particular, for full-domain HRS codes with low multiplicity, the triangular transformations reduce to diagonal scalings, and the Euclidean dual is obtained as the row reversal of an HRS code. Based on this reverse-order dual structure, we further study reverse self-dual HRS codes. We establish explicit criteria for reverse self-duality and construct several families from additive and multiplicative coset structures.
tldr: This paper studies duality and self-dual constructions for hyperderivative Reed-Solomon codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman metric.
motivation: To understand the dual structure of HRS codes, which are a generalization of Reed-Solomon codes, and to construct reverse self-dual HRS codes.
method: Uses a residue-theoretic argument to derive an explicit component-wise representation of the Euclidean dual of an HRS code, and then establishes criteria for reverse self-duality.
result: The Euclidean dual of an HRS code is blockwise upper-triangularly equivalent to a reverse-order HRS evaluation code; for full-domain low-multiplicity codes, the dual is a row reversal of an HRS code. Families of reverse self-dual HRS codes are constructed.
conclusion: The dual of an HRS code is not generally an HRS code but has a structured form, enabling the construction of reverse self-dual codes.

title: Spatial Semantic Communication: When Semantic Transmission Meets Index Modulation
authors: Xinghao Guo, Yin Xu, Dazhi He, Hanjiang Hong, Zhiyong Chen, Cixiao Zhang, Yiyan Wu, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current digital semantic communication systems have primarily focused on maintaining compatibility with conventional constellation-based modulation. In contrast, index modulation (IM) represents a more spectrally and energy-efficient alternative by exploiting additional dimensions for information conveyance. Recognizing this potential, this paper bridges the gap between IM and semantic communications by proposing a novel spatial semantic communication (SSC) system leveraging cutting-edge fluid antenna-IM (FA-IM) technology. Compatible with existing joint source-channel coding (JSCC) architectures, the proposed SSC system employs the residual quantization (RQ) approach to discretize analog semantic features for subsequent digital IM transmission. Notably, the proposed SSC system synergizes RQ and IM via a semantic-aware stream splitting scheme, which ensures that critical semantic information undergoes less severe channel fading, thereby further optimizing semantic transmission performance. Simulation results validate that the proposed SSC system effectively integrates the high fidelity of RQ, the reliability of semantic-aware splitting, and the spatial efficiency of FA-IM, thereby providing a robust solution for future digital semantic transmission. The open source code is available at: [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a spatial semantic communication system that integrates index modulation with joint source-channel coding for efficient digital semantic transmission.
motivation: Current digital semantic communication systems rely on conventional constellation-based modulation, which is less spectrally and energy-efficient than index modulation.
method: The system uses fluid antenna index modulation (FA-IM) and residual quantization (RQ) to discretize analog semantic features, with a semantic-aware stream splitting scheme to protect critical information.
result: Simulations show that the proposed system achieves high fidelity, reliability, and spatial efficiency, outperforming traditional approaches.
conclusion: The SSC system provides a robust solution for future digital semantic transmission by synergizing RQ, semantic-aware splitting, and FA-IM.

title: Examining Qrmi As A Unified Interface For Quantum-HPC Integration
authors: Thomas Badts (pasqal), Tim Boyle (national Quantum Computing Centre), Claudio Carvalho (IBM), Antonio C\'orcoles (IBM), Andrew Damin (rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Vadim Elisseev (IBM), Jonathan Frassineti (CINECA), Daniel Gruber (HPC Gridware), Hiroshi Horii (IBM), Eun-Kyung Lee (IBM), James Machin (alice & Bob), Sara Marzella (CINECA), Mateusz Meller (STFC Hartree Centre), Daniel Milroy (lawrence Livermore National Laboratory), Matthieu Moreau (pasqal), Munetaka Ohtani (IBM), Elisabeth Ortega-Carrasco (qilimanjaro Quantum Tech), Doug Oucharek (oak Ridge National Laboratory), Yoonho Park (IBM), Adarsh Patil (siemens), Emre M. Sahin (STFC Hartree Centre), G\'abor Samu (IBM), Seetharami Seelam (IBM), Amir Shehata (oak Ridge National Laboratory), Vanessa Sochat (lawrence Livermore National Laboratory), James Thorne (national Quantum Computing Centre), Oscar Wallis (STFC Hartree Centre), Aleksander Wennersteen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The efficient and scalable integration of quantum resources into high-performance computing (HPC) environments requires standardized mechanisms for resource management, scheduling, and workflow orchestration across diverse and heterogeneous infrastructures. The Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) addresses this challenge through a thin, vendor-agnostic middleware layer that provides standardized APIs for scheduling, executing, and monitoring quantum workloads while exposing quantum resources as first-class schedulable resources alongside CPUs and GPUs. Although previous work demonstrated QRMI integration with the Slurm workload manager, its applicability across other workload managers remained unexamined. This paper extends the validation of QRMI to a broad range of workload managers, including PBS, LSF, Grid Engine, Kubernetes, and the Flux Framework, encompassing traditional batch schedulers, a cloud-native orchestration platform, and a graph-based scheduler. We examine the integration patterns, implementation requirements, and scheduler-specific considerations associated with each environment and compare QRMI with alternative approaches to quantum resource integration. We demonstrate that QRMI provides a portable and flexible abstraction layer that minimizes scheduler-specific modifications while enabling consistent access to heterogeneous quantum resources across both on-premises and cloud environments.
tldr: This paper validates the Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) across multiple workload managers for quantum-HPC integration.
motivation: Efficient integration of quantum resources into HPC environments requires standardized resource management and scheduling mechanisms.
method: The authors extend QRMI validation to various workload managers (PBS, LSF, Grid Engine, Kubernetes, Flux Framework) and compare integration patterns.
result: QRMI provides a portable abstraction layer that minimizes scheduler-specific modifications while enabling consistent access to heterogeneous quantum resources.
conclusion: QRMI is a viable middleware for quantum-HPC integration across diverse HPC environments.

title: Information Propagation And Contraction In Functional Interpretations
authors: Chuangjie Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper separates two components of functional interpretations: affine information propagation and contraction. We introduce information nuclei as an algebraic interface to capture the affine component. An information nucleus specifies what information is associated with finite-type objects, how exact objects are compatible with such information, and how information is propagated through functions. From any information nucleus we obtain a formula translation and a soundness theorem for affine finite-type arithmetic. Extending soundness to finite-type arithmetic with contraction requires one additional ingredient: a formula-indexed contraction structure reducing the challenges generated by duplicated assumptions to a single challenge. Finite collections of candidates with union yield a Herbrand-style interpretation, while exact information with challenge selection yields the usual Dialectica interpretation over an arithmetic system restricted to decidable primitive formulas. The resulting framework provides a uniform method for specifying the information carried by extracted realizers, allowing existing functional interpretations to be systematically enriched with auxiliary data, such as continuity information.
tldr: This paper develops a framework for functional interpretations in logic, separating affine information propagation and contraction.
motivation: To provide a uniform method for specifying information carried by extracted realizers in functional interpretations, enabling systematic enrichment with auxiliary data.
method: Introduces information nuclei as an algebraic interface for affine information propagation, and formula-indexed contraction structures to handle contraction in finite-type arithmetic.
result: The framework yields a Herbrand-style interpretation and a Dialectica interpretation over decidable primitive formulas, allowing enrichment with continuity information.
conclusion: The work offers a modular approach to functional interpretations but is primarily a contribution to proof theory and logic, not directly related to quantum information theory or the other specified directions.

title: Quantum Term Rewrite Systems: Applications To Complexity Analysis
authors: Kostia Chardonnet, Emmanuel Hainry, Romain P\'echoux, Thomas Vinet
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Term Rewrite Systems (TRS) is a computational model offering a level of abstraction well-suited towards static analysis, e.g., termination or complexity analyses. In this paper, we introduce Quantum Term Rewrite Systems (QTRS), an extension of TRS to quantum computing, thus allowing to benefit from quantum advantage while being able to certify the complexity. We ensure that QTRS correspond to physically realizable processes and adapt techniques to obtain termination certificates or generic bounds on the reduction length. We delineate a class of terminating QTRS that can be compiled to uniform families of quantum circuits of size bounded by the reduction length. Conversely, this class is universal for quantum circuits. In particular, we show a characterization of the class of functions computable in quantum polynomial time, known as [MATH].
tldr: This paper extends term rewrite systems to quantum computing for complexity analysis, but does not align with the user's research directions.
motivation: The authors aim to combine quantum computing with term rewrite systems to certify complexity and termination, leveraging quantum advantage.
method: They introduce Quantum Term Rewrite Systems (QTRS), define a class of terminating QTRS that can be compiled to uniform families of quantum circuits, and show universality for quantum circuits.
result: The paper characterizes the class of functions computable in quantum polynomial time using QTRS.
conclusion: QTRS provide a framework for complexity analysis of quantum algorithms, but the work is more about computational models than the user's specific interests.

title: Dynamic Logic With Parallel Operator For Verifying Communication Protocols
authors: Mario R. F. Benevides Luiz C. F. Fernandez (federal University Of Rio de Janeiro)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a dynamic logic with parallel operators for the formal verification of authenticity and safety properties of cryptographic protocols. The logic incorporates communication actions and is specifically designed to reason about protocol executions in adversarial environments. We extend an existing dynamic logic with parallel operators by introducing concepts derived from the Dolev-Yao intruder model. As the underlying logic is completely axiomatizable, we obtain a complete axiomatization for the extended system. Furthermore, we develop a tableau calculus for the proposed logic and prove its termination, soundness, and completeness.
tldr: This paper presents a dynamic logic with parallel operators for verifying communication protocols, focusing on cryptographic protocol security.
motivation: To formally verify authenticity and safety properties of cryptographic protocols in adversarial environments using a logical framework.
method: Extends an existing dynamic logic with parallel operators and incorporates concepts from the Dolev-Yao intruder model, providing a complete axiomatization and a tableau calculus.
result: Obtains a complete axiomatization for the extended system and proves termination, soundness, and completeness of the tableau calculus.
conclusion: The proposed logic enables formal verification of communication protocols, but the work is primarily in logic and protocol verification, not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

title: From Dag-Like Proofs To Boolean Circuits In Lean
authors: Edward Hermann Haeusler Lorenzo Saraiva (pontificia Universidade Catolica Do Rio de Janeiro)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we present a method for encoding Dag-Like Derivability Structures (DLDS), obtained via horizontal compression of Natural Deduction proofs in purely implicational minimal logic, as Boolean circuits. These DLDS compress Natural Deduction tree-like proofs into directed acyclic graphs, preserving logical correctness while reducing redundancy. We formally define the circuit construction process and establish its pointwise correctness, showing that, for any fixed path assignment, the resulting Boolean circuit agrees with the intended dependency-propagation semantics. A Lean formalization establishes machine-checked guarantees for the circuit evaluator and includes a restricted bridge for the uncompressed simple-tree fragment, connecting valid DLDS instances in that fragment to genuine circuit acceptance of their extracted paths under the route and discharge conditions formalized in Lean. This approach opens new perspectives for automated theorem proving and formal certification.
tldr: This paper encodes Dag-Like Derivability Structures from natural deduction proofs into Boolean circuits and formalizes the construction in Lean.
motivation: To reduce redundancy in natural deduction proofs and enable automated theorem proving with machine-checked guarantees.
method: The authors define a horizontal compression of tree-like proofs into directed acyclic graphs (DLDS) and then construct Boolean circuits from these DLDS, proving pointwise correctness.
result: A Lean formalization provides machine-checked guarantees for the circuit evaluator and a restricted bridge for the simple-tree fragment.
conclusion: This approach opens new perspectives for automated theorem proving and formal certification, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…

tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new magnetic phase combining zero net magnetization with spin-split bands.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied in periodic crystals; extending it to quasicrystals explores new symmetry-breaking mechanisms and potential spintronic applications.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to compute electronic structure and spin polarization, analyzing the role of quasicrystalline symmetries.
result: They find that quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order with spin-split bands despite the lack of translational symmetry, driven by local cluster symmetries.
conclusion: Quasicrystals provide a new platform for altermagnetism, expanding the material landscape for spintronics and fundamental magnetism studies.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a minimal negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combination of mean-field ODEs and particle-based simulations.
motivation: Oscillations are a hallmark of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors analyze a degradation-mediated negative feedback loop by coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with particle-based simulations to capture phase separation effects.
result: Phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, altering the dynamics compared to the well-mixed case.
conclusion: Phase separation is a key mechanism that can generate oscillatory behavior in negative feedback loops, relevant to biological nonequilibrium processes.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and other numerical techniques to compute spin correlations and charge order.
result: They find that magnetic correlations are suppressed with doping and that stripe-like charge order emerges.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the phase diagram of SU(3) Hubbard models and guide future experiments.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, and Michele Casula

[MATH] sulfur hydride has been widely investigated for its high superconducting critical temperature [MATH] of 203 K at about [MATH]. Despite being the precursor of superconducting hydrides, a detailed picture of its structural phase diagra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on its structural phase diagram and high-temperature superconductivity.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase diagram of H3S is crucial for explaining its high superconducting critical temperature, but the detailed mechanism remains unclear.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and anharmonic phonon theory to study the structural phase transition and quantum critical behavior in H3S.
result: They identify a displacive quantum critical point that influences the superconducting properties, providing insights into the phase diagram.
conclusion: The displacive quantum critical point plays a key role in the high-Tc superconductivity of H3S, offering a new perspective on hydride superconductors.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, and Xiaoguang Ma

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, focusing on relaxation and configurational entropy.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, exploring the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation time.
method: Extracting spin configurations from a buckled colloidal monolayer and analyzing configurational entropy and relaxation times.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is found.
conclusion: The work provides insights into glassy dynamics in spin systems but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: Understanding the short-distance behavior of confining strings in non-Abelian gauge theories is important for connecting perturbative and non-perturbative regimes.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator by summing over closed flux tube exchanges and analyze the leading divergence at short separations using perturbative methods.
result: They find that the leading divergence is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, providing a link between the string tension and the running coupling.
conclusion: The results demonstrate how asymptotic freedom leaves an imprint on the properties of confining strings, offering insights into the transition from perturbative to confining physics.

title: Integrated Soliton Microcombs Beyond The Turnkey Limit
authors: Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Self-injection locking enables integrated soliton microcombs with turnkey initiation and improved coherence, but it also pins the pump close to resonance, limiting the access to large detuning for broader combs. Here, we use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043802] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated soliton microcomb platform that uses an auxiliary resonator to achieve broader frequency combs beyond the turnkey limit.
motivation: Integrated soliton microcombs are limited in bandwidth because self-injection locking pins the pump near resonance, preventing access to large detunings needed for broader combs.
method: The authors use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adiabatic frequency tuning across a wide range while maintaining turnkey initiation and low phase noise.
result: They achieve soliton microcombs with significantly broader bandwidth than conventional turnkey designs, demonstrating improved coherence and stability.
conclusion: This approach advances integrated photonic frequency comb technology, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-feng Yang, and Shuigang Xu

The interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons gives rise to exotic quantum states in condensed matter systems. Here, we demonstrate an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, achieved by controlling the Kondo hybridization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046301] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a heavy-fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, driven by Kondo hybridization.
motivation: To explore the interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons in a tunable graphene platform.
method: Electrical transport measurements on magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene with controlled doping and magnetic field.
result: Demonstration of an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram, including Kondo screening and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Twisted trilayer graphene provides a new platform for studying heavy-fermion physics and correlated electron states.

title: Deep-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian In Real Space
authors: Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, and Yong Xu

Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem. Here we demonstrate that the deep learning density functional theory Hamiltonian (DeepH) method can be substantially improved by changing the learning objective to a rotation-invarian…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046401] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict density functional theory Hamiltonians in real space, improving accuracy with rotation-invariant features.
motivation: Integrating physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical problem for efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations.
method: The authors modify the DeepH method to learn a rotation-invariant representation of the Hamiltonian, using neural networks to map atomic configurations to Hamiltonian matrices.
result: The improved method achieves higher accuracy and better transferability across different materials compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that incorporating physical symmetries into deep learning models significantly enhances performance in predicting electronic structure Hamiltonians.

title: Bridging Constrained Random-Phase Approximation And Linear Response Theory For Computing Hubbard Parameters
authors: Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, and Claude Ederer

The predictive accuracy of popular extensions to density-functional theory (DFT) such as [MATH] and DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory ([MATH]) hinges on using realistic values for the screened Coulomb interaction [MATH]. Here, we present a systematic comparison of the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046503] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares methods for computing Hubbard U parameters in DFT+U and DFT+DMFT, focusing on constrained random-phase approximation and linear response theory.
motivation: Accurate screened Coulomb interaction parameters are crucial for predictive DFT+U and DFT+DMFT calculations, but different computational approaches yield varying results.
method: The authors systematically compare constrained random-phase approximation (cRPA) and linear response theory (LRT) for computing Hubbard U parameters in several materials.
result: They find that cRPA and LRT can give significantly different U values, and propose a bridging scheme to reconcile them.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for choosing and validating Hubbard U parameters in correlated materials simulations.

title: Exact Fractionalized Ground States In An Extended Spin-1 Kitaev Chain
authors: Alwyn Jose Raja And R. Ganesh
abstract:
Author(s): Alwyn Jose Raja and R. Ganesh

Inspired by the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) model, we present exact solutions for a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings. We consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms. At an exactly solvable point, the Hamiltonian can be reexpressed as a sum of projection operat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046701] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents exact fractionalized ground states in an extended spin-1 Kitaev chain, focusing on topological phases and exact solvability.
motivation: The work is inspired by the AKLT model and aims to find exact solutions for spin-1 chains with Kitaev-like couplings, exploring fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms and reexpress the Hamiltonian as a sum of projection operators at an exactly solvable point.
result: They obtain exact ground states that exhibit fractionalization, analogous to the AKLT model.
conclusion: The study provides a new exactly solvable model in condensed matter physics, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Chiral Magnon Mixing By Symmetry-Breaking In Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, And R. J. Mcqueeney
abstract:
Author(s): Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, and R. J. McQueeney

Magnons in ferromagnets possess spin angular momentum defined by right-handed precession of the moment around the magnetization direction. In antiferromagnets with no net magnetization, left- and right-handed magnons are degenerate in the absence of an applied field. Ferrimagnets possess uncompensat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046702] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral magnon mixing due to symmetry-breaking in collinear ferrimagnets using neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand how symmetry-breaking in ferrimagnets affects magnon chirality and mixing, which is important for spintronics and magnonics.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a collinear ferrimagnet, combined with theoretical modeling, to observe and analyze magnon modes.
result: Observation of chiral magnon mixing induced by symmetry-breaking, leading to non-degenerate left- and right-handed magnon modes.
conclusion: Symmetry-breaking in ferrimagnets can control magnon chirality, offering potential for spintronic applications.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, and Jian-Wei Pan

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns and short-range correlations in fermionic Hubbard gases after ballistic expansion from optical lattices.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems through interference patterns is important, but the focus is on ultracold atom physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors experimentally observe interference of ultracold fermionic atoms released from optical lattices and analyze the resulting patterns to extract correlation information.
result: They demonstrate that interference patterns encode short-range correlations in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into strongly correlated fermionic systems but does not directly advance quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space groups.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify this possibility.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, meaning it does not behave as a switchable order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality should not be classified as a ferroic property in the context of structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space groups.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, and Agustin Palacios-Laloy

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer, focusing on sensor performance rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding noise sources in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving sensitivity in magnetic field measurements.
method: The authors experimentally characterize noise contributions in a single-beam vector magnetometer using metastable helium-4, analyzing various operating regimes.
result: The sensor achieves vector magnetic readings with noise below 30 fT/√Hz in optimal conditions, and the main noise origins are identified.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive noise model for this type of magnetometer, aiding in future sensor optimization.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, and M. Pittman

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports progress toward measuring the quantum-noise-limited optical nonlinearity of vacuum, a test of quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium under intense electromagnetic fields; measuring this effect would confirm a fundamental prediction.
method: The authors use intense ultrashort laser pulses in an interferometric setup to detect the deflection of light by light, aiming to achieve quantum-noise-limited sensitivity.
result: The paper describes experimental progress and setup details but does not report a definitive measurement of vacuum nonlinearity.
conclusion: The work advances toward a measurement of vacuum nonlinearity but has not yet achieved the target sensitivity or confirmed the effect.

title: Quantum-to-semiclassical Husimi Dynamics Of non-Hermitian Localization Transitions
authors: Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, And Ranjan Modak
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, and Ranjan Modak

The localization transition in the Hermitian Aubry-André model is known to have a classical origin, with the critical point being exactly predictable from an analysis of classical phase-space trajectories. Motivated by this correspondence, we investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013318] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in a non-Hermitian Aubry-André model using Husimi dynamics, finding that the transition is not predictable from classical phase-space analysis.
motivation: To understand whether the localization transition in non-Hermitian systems has a classical origin, as it does in the Hermitian Aubry-André model.
method: The authors analyze the Husimi distribution and its dynamics for the non-Hermitian model, comparing with classical phase-space trajectories.
result: The non-Hermitian localization transition does not correspond to a classical phase-space transition; the critical point cannot be predicted from classical analysis.
conclusion: The classical origin of localization is lost in non-Hermitian systems, highlighting a fundamental difference from the Hermitian case.

title: Optimization Of Two-photon Excitation By Indistinguishable Photons In A Three-level Atom
authors: Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, And Anita Dąbrowska

We investigate the excitation of a three-level ladder-type atom by a unidirectional field with a pair of indistinguishable photons. Starting from an analytical expression for the two-photon absorption probability, we determine the two-photon state that maximizes the population of the upper atomic st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013717] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes two-photon excitation in a three-level atom using indistinguishable photons.
motivation: To understand and maximize the excitation probability of a three-level atom by a pair of indistinguishable photons.
method: Analytical derivation of two-photon absorption probability and optimization of the two-photon state.
result: Determined the optimal two-photon state that maximizes upper state population.
conclusion: The work provides insights into light-matter interaction at the quantum level, but is not directly relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on the limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, analyzing the validity of the far-off-resonance approximation.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is found to be inadequate for describing ETPA in cesium atoms under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve discrepancies in ETPA, but accurate modeling requires going beyond the far-off-resonance approximation.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, and Yueming Zhou

We investigate theoretically the coherent dynamics of helium photoionization driven by a pair of time-delayed laser pulses using the [MATH]-dimensional two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Our numerical calculations reveal that the resulting photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed laser pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is fundamental for quantum control and attosecond science.
method: Numerically solves the two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium under a pair of time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly dips, indicating entanglement between the ion and photoelectron, and the entanglement can be controlled by the pulse delay.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses provide a means to control ion-photoelectron entanglement, which may have implications for quantum information but is primarily a strong-field physics result.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets using density functional theory.
motivation: To understand wetting and formation of free-standing shell-shaped quantum droplets in three-component Bose mixtures.
method: A density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections.
result: The analysis predicts conditions for wetting and the formation of shell-shaped droplets.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum fluid wetting but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, and B. Prasanna Venkatesh

We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful dynamical probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013314] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate by suddenly changing the polarization direction of magnetic dipole moments.
motivation: To probe superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs using a sudden change in polarization direction as a dynamical probe.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the response of a dipolar BEC to a sudden small angular deviation of the polarization direction, examining the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the dynamical response reveals signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in different phases of the dipolar BEC.
conclusion: The sudden polarization change serves as a useful dynamical probe to sense superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling-induced Geometric Squeezing In Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, And Li Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, and Li Chen

Squeezed states play a key role in diverse frontiers of quantum physics. Geometrically squeezed states, squeezed states in the orbital phase space of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), have been conventionally generated by anisotropic-trapping potentials. In this work, we propose a different…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013316] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating geometric squeezed states in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates via spin-orbit coupling instead of anisotropic trapping.
motivation: Geometric squeezing in rotating BECs is conventionally achieved with anisotropic traps; this work explores an alternative mechanism using spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a rotating BEC with spin-orbit coupling, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the squeezing parameter in the orbital phase space.
result: Spin-orbit coupling can induce geometric squeezing comparable to or exceeding that from anisotropic traps, with tunable parameters.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling offers a new route to generate squeezed states in rotating BECs, which may benefit quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Optical Repumping And Controlled Population Transfer In A Two-color Magneto-optical Trap
authors: Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, And Philippe Wilhelm Courteille
abstract:
Author(s): Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, and Philippe Wilhelm Courteille

We study a repumping transition for [MATH] atoms trapped in a blue magneto-optical trap. We show that, while the repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than for traditional schemes, it is sufficient for recycling all atoms, provided the repumping laser beams are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013715] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an optical repumping scheme for atoms in a two-color magneto-optical trap, focusing on experimental efficiency and population transfer.
motivation: To improve repumping efficiency in magneto-optical traps for better atom trapping and cooling.
method: Experimental study of a repumping transition using two-color laser beams and measurement of repumping efficiency.
result: The repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than traditional schemes but sufficient for recycling all atoms.
conclusion: The proposed repumping scheme is viable for atom trapping despite lower efficiency.

title: Dynamics Of A Generalized Photonic Lattice Via Driven Tight-binding Models
authors: Xiyu Guan And Zhiyong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyu Guan and Zhiyong Zhao

Conventional photonic waveguide arrays provide a compact and stable platform for simulating condensed-matter systems, enabling the direct observation of coherent quantum phenomena through optical waves. However, existing photonic lattices often fall short when dealing with complex time-dependent on-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of a generalized photonic lattice using driven tight-binding models, focusing on optical wave propagation in time-dependent photonic structures.
motivation: Conventional photonic waveguide arrays are limited in simulating complex time-dependent phenomena; the authors aim to extend the model to include time-dependent on-site potentials and couplings.

method: Derives normal and anomalous proper polarization functions and screened Coulomb interactions in a two-dimensional superfluid electron-hole bilayer at zero temperature, modifying the self-consistent field approach.

conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Electron-plasmon Coupling In The Layered Transition Metal Dichalcogenide ${\mathrm{ZrSe}}_{2−x}{\mathrm{Te}}_{x}$
authors: Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, And Juan Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, and Juan Jiang

Electron-plasmon coupling, in which carriers are dressed by collective electronic oscillations, represents an important many-body interaction in solids. Here, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we report the tunable electron-plasmon coupling in the layered transition metal dichalcogeni…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports tunable electron-plasmon coupling in a layered transition metal dichalcogenide using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Electron-plasmon coupling is an important many-body interaction in solids, and tuning it in layered materials could enable new physics.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to study the electronic structure of ZrSe2-xTex alloys.
result: The electron-plasmon coupling strength can be tuned by varying the tellurium concentration.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a tunable many-body interaction in a 2D material, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Current-induced Spin-orbit Torque On The Surface Of A Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Connected To The Two-dimensional Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}$: Effects Of Twisting And Gating
authors: Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, And Reza Asgari
abstract:
Author(s): Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, and Reza Asgari

Motivated by recent progress in employing two key classes of two-dimensional materials—topological insulators and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs)—as spin sources for generating spin-orbit torque (SOT), we investigate current-induced spin polarization and the resulting SOT in bilayers compos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045422] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies current-induced spin-orbit torque in TMDC/ferromagnet bilayers, focusing on twisting and gating effects.
motivation: To understand spin-orbit torque generation in two-dimensional heterostructures for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model and linear response theory to compute spin polarization and torque as functions of twist angle and gate voltage.
