conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to be a rich field with broad applications, and interdisciplinary collaboration remains essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in molecular systems, and understanding its theoretical description is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are diverse and can be applied to photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results or deep connections to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum technologies.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities in quantum information processing, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can directly access atomic-scale disorder information in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a more complete picture of defects, aiding materials science.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, by searching for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions are a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but current experiments have not yet found evidence for such interactions beyond the standard model.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why clarifies the limits of thermodynamics and enables design of materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that violations occur when measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity, and shows how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The apparent violations do not contradict thermodynamics but rather highlight the importance of assumptions; this understanding can guide development of materials with properties beyond classical limits.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional simulations across platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic geometries open new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics beyond conventional setups.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement tests) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement, but no conclusive evidence has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory and can be reproduced classically, suggesting broader implications for foundations of physics and philosophy.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend paradox is a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other puzzles like the Boltzmann brain problem.
method: The authors analyze extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, construct classical thought experiments with agent duplication, and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the core difficulty is a limitation of probabilistic descriptions of observations across agents.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, addressing issues of private versus intersubjective verification in science.

title: Superluminal Transformations And Indeterminism
authors: Amrapali Sen And Flavio Del Santo
abstract: Quantum theory is widely regarded as fundamentally indeterministic, yet classical frameworks can also exhibit indeterminism once infinite information is abandoned. At the same time, relativity is usually taken to forbid superluminal signalling, although Lorentz symmetry formally admits superluminal transformations (SpTs). Dragan and Ekert have argued that SpTs entail a form of indeterminism analogous to that encountered in quantum theory. Here, we derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from a set of natural assumptions: any framework admitting non-order-preserving SpTs must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon the notion that time determines a preferred causal ordering. In particular, one possible implication is that any theory accommodating SpTs suggests an ontology with unbounded informational content, akin to deterministic classical theories formulated over the real numbers. Consequently, any ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information.
tldr: The paper explores the connection between superluminal transformations and indeterminism, deriving a no-go theorem that challenges the idea that finite information can account for ontic indeterminacy.
motivation: To understand whether superluminal transformations can lead to indeterminism analogous to quantum theory, and to examine the implications for foundational physics.
method: The authors derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from a set of natural assumptions about time ordering, information content, and causality.
result: Any theory admitting non-order-preserving superluminal transformations must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon time-determined causal ordering.
conclusion: Ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information, suggesting that such theories require unbounded informational content.

title: Wave Packet Motion In A Quantized Electromagnetic Field: Analytic Results
authors: Szabolcs Hack, Béla Gábor Pusztai, Krisztina Joós, Sándor Varró, Attila Czirják And Péter Földi
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a multimode quantized electromagnetic field and obtain an analytic solution for the full electron-field system. In the present finite-mode formulation the total electron-field dynamics remains closed and unitary. The framework enables the calculation of position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states, allowing us to identify quantum corrections to the corresponding classical motion. While the corrections to the position expectation value are weak and largely insensitive to the quantum state of the field, the wave packet broadening exhibits a pronounced dependence on the field state. In particular, the quantum uncertainty of the radiation is directly imprinted onto the spatial uncertainty of the particle. We illustrate these effects for Gaussian wave packets interacting with coherent, Fock, and squeezed states, including bright squeezed vacuum. The interaction with a finite-duration laser pulse is also analyzed as a multimode example. Our results provide a transparent analytic route toward understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings.
tldr: This paper analytically solves the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a quantized electromagnetic field, showing how quantum field fluctuations affect electron motion.
motivation: Understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings is important for fundamental physics and applications like attosecond science.
method: The authors derive an analytic solution for the full electron-field system in a finite-mode formulation, computing position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states.
result: Quantum corrections to the position expectation value are weak and insensitive to the field state, but wave packet broadening strongly depends on the field state, with quantum uncertainty of the radiation imprinted onto the particle's spatial uncertainty.
conclusion: The results provide a transparent analytic route to understanding quantum light–electron interactions, with implications for strong-field physics and quantum optics.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions with highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and magnetometry applications.
motivation: To understand alignment tensor contributions in highly polarized 3He ensembles, which are not captured by traditional orientation-based models, and to improve precision measurements.
method: A linearized mean-field model is developed to describe alignment tensor effects, and free-induction-decay measurements are performed to observe the dependence on nuclear polarization.
result: A pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is observed in the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensemble response, and good agreement between experiment and theory is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures around optical vortices, focusing on meronic defects and subwavelength confinement.
motivation: To understand and characterize the unique spin structures that decorate phase singularities in paraxial vortex beams.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin field topology using the spin unit sphere and transverse-axial Poincaré sphere, with numerical simulations of propagation and robustness.
result: The spin field forms a non-spreading meronic texture with deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line, exhibiting enhanced robustness against perturbations.
conclusion: These topological spin defects are intrinsic to optical vortices and may have applications in robust optical manipulation or information transfer.

title: Observation Of Floquet Tensor Monopoles
authors: Hao Yuan, Weixuan Zhang, Na Sun And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract: Tensor monopoles, topological singularities of Kalb–Ramond tensor gauge fields, have garnered widespread attention in high-energy and condensed matter physics. They give rise to exotic phenomena such as quantized magnetoelectric responses and chiral boundary states, acting as potential building blocks for the development of topological devices in high-dimensional space. However, theoretical studies and experimental realizations reported to date have remained in static settings, and the realization of Floquet tensor monopoles (FTMs) and their associated anomalous non-equilibrium topological features has yet to be achieved. Here, we report the first theoretical and experimental implementation of FTMs in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system. We systematically uncover the driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of FTMs, together with their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence. These phenomena are unique to FTMs and have no static counterparts. In experiments, we design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits, and directly observe the controllable motion of FTMs in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency. Our findings extend tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a theoretical and experimental platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying the groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental observation of Floquet tensor monopoles in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system using time-varying topological circuits.
motivation: Tensor monopoles have been studied in static settings, but their non-equilibrium counterparts and associated anomalous topological features had not been realized.
method: The authors design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits to realize a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, and tune the driving frequency to control the creation, motion, and annihilation of Floquet tensor monopoles.
result: They directly observe the controllable motion of Floquet tensor monopoles in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states.
conclusion: This work extends tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime and provides a platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Magnon Dynamics
authors: Xi-Guang Wang And Jamal Berakdar
abstract: A defining quantity of a physical system is its energy which is represented by the Hamiltonian. In closed quantum mechanical or/and fully coherent wave-based systems the Hamiltonian is introduced as a Hermitian operator which ensures real energy spectrum and secures the decomposition of any state over a complete basis set that spans the space where states live. Pseudo-Hermitian, or PT symmetric, systems are a special class of non-Hermitian ones. They describe open systems but may still have real energy spectrum. The eigenmodes are however not orthogonal in general. This qualitative difference to Hermitian physics has a range of consequences for the physical behavior of the system in the steady state or when it is subjected to external perturbations. This overview reviews the recent progress in the field of pseudo-Hermitian physics as it unfolds when applied to low-energy excitations of magnetically ordered materials. The focus is mainly on long wavelength spin excitations (spin waves) with magnons being the energy quanta of these excitations. Various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures with different types of coupling to the environments as well as spatio-temporally engineered systems will be discussed with a focus on the particular aspects that are brought about by the pseudo-Hermiticity such as mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric assisted Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and field-induced enhanced sensitivity.
tldr: A review of pseudo-Hermitian magnon dynamics in magnetically ordered materials, focusing on non-Hermitian effects such as mode amplification and non-reciprocal propagation.
motivation: To explore the unique physics of pseudo-Hermitian systems in the context of magnonics, which may lead to novel functionalities like cloaking and enhanced sensitivity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental progress on pseudo-Hermitian magnon systems, covering various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and hybrid structures.
result: Pseudo-Hermiticity enables phenomena such as non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, and PT-symmetric Floquet engineering.
conclusion: Pseudo-Hermitian magnonics is a rapidly developing field with potential applications in wave-based information processing, but it is not directly aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of master stability functions for analyzing synchronization stability in complex networks, covering pairwise, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) is a powerful tool, but a systematic review across various network types is lacking.
method: The paper formulates the MSF framework for undirected, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks, and provides numerical analysis and algorithms for computing MSF and classifying stability regimes.
result: A unified and simplified MSF analysis is presented for various networked systems, with algorithms for computing MSF and identifying stability regimes.
conclusion: The review makes the MSF tool more accessible and highlights underexplored areas, such as using machine learning to estimate MSF.

title: Classification And Correlation Signatures Of Chiral Spin Liquids On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Leon Balents And Yasir Iqbal Chunxiao Liu
abstract: We present a systematic classification and variational study of chiral quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice based on fermionic parton constructions. Focusing on chiral and spin-liquid Ansätze, we characterize their symmetry properties, flux structures, and low-energy spinon spectra within a projective symmetry group framework, and incorporate gauge fluctuations through Gutzwiller-projected wave functions studied by variational Monte Carlo. From the equal-time spin structure factor, we develop correlation-based diagnostics that distinguish gauge-dominated Coulomb phases from states with substantial matter-field and short-range contributions. Distinct chiral flux sectors, though close in energy, exhibit markedly different degrees of emergent gauge-field dominance, reflected in the geometry and contrast of pinch-point singularities. Although these states are not competitive ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model, they define a physically meaningful family of proximate chiral phases relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.
tldr: This paper classifies chiral spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice using parton constructions and variational Monte Carlo, focusing on symmetry and correlation signatures.
motivation: Chiral spin liquids are exotic quantum phases with potential applications in topological quantum computation, but their classification on the pyrochlore lattice is incomplete.
method: The authors use fermionic parton theory with projective symmetry groups to classify chiral Ansätze, and study Gutzwiller-projected wave functions via variational Monte Carlo to compute spin structure factors.
result: They identify distinct chiral flux sectors with different degrees of gauge-field dominance, reflected in pinch-point singularities, though these states are not ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model.
conclusion: The work provides a family of proximate chiral phases relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Synthesizing Superoscillations With Just Two Frequencies
authors: Diyar Talbayev Denys I. Bondar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superoscillations, band-limited signals that locally oscillate faster than their highest Fourier component, have recently enabled superspectroscopy and super-sensing. Previous experiments [Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 153803 (2023), [URL] and APL Photonics 10, 086107 (2025), [URL] relied on combining four quasi-sinusoidal harmonics to generate temporal superoscillations. Here, we show that just two harmonics are sufficient to produce superoscillations of comparable quality, as quantified by the local frequency. By reanalyzing prior experimental data with two harmonics (0.5 and 0.6 THz) and performing new experiments with 0.9 and 1 THz harmonics, we demonstrate a twofold enhancement in local frequency relative to the highest frequency component -- matching the enhancement previously achieved with four harmonics. We provide a simple analytical explanation for the bichromatic superoscillations based on near-complete destructive interference, and identify an optimal frequency separation of approximately 10% that balances the superoscillatory frequency enhancement against signal amplitude. This simplification substantially lowers the experimental barrier to implementing superoscillation-based technology.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that superoscillations can be synthesized using just two frequencies, achieving comparable quality to previous four-frequency experiments.
motivation: Superoscillations enable super-resolution sensing and spectroscopy, but previous implementations required multiple harmonics, increasing experimental complexity. The authors aim to simplify the generation of superoscillations.
method: The authors reanalyze prior experimental data and perform new experiments using two harmonics (0.5/0.6 THz and 0.9/1 THz), and provide an analytical explanation based on near-complete destructive interference.
result: Bichromatic superoscillations achieve a twofold enhancement in local frequency relative to the highest frequency component, matching the enhancement previously achieved with four harmonics. An optimal frequency separation of ~10% is identified.
conclusion: Superoscillations can be generated with just two frequencies, significantly lowering the experimental barrier for superoscillation-based technologies.

title: Controllable Localization And Manipulation Of Optical Hollow Traps By Means Of Optical-vortex Diffraction
authors: O. V. Angelsky, A. Y. Bekshaev, C. Y. Zenkova, I. I. Mokhun, X. Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An optical vortex (OV) is coupled with the local intensity zero and is thus a field configuration suitable for "hollow" optical traps and optical tweezers. When an incident circular OV beam experiences diffraction at a rectilinear screen edge (SE), and the conditions of weak diffraction perturbation (the SE is far enough from the beam axis) are fulfilled, the main consequence is the OV-core displacement from its initial (axial) position. Based on the model of incident Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beam, we investigate analytically and numerically the ways of controlling the OV-core position in the diffracted-field cross section by means of changing the SE position with respect to the incident-beam axis. The results show that regulating the SE position with ~1 mcm accuracy (which is available for existing mechanical tools), controllable OV-core motion with a sub-nanometer accuracy can be realized. Possible modifications of this motion depending on the incident beam topological charge, wavefront curvature, SE properties (semitransparent screen, phase-step screen) and the distance between the diffraction plane and the observation plane are analyzed. The conditions most favorable for the micro-object trapping and manipulation are specified and discussed.
tldr: This paper studies the controllable displacement of an optical vortex core via diffraction at a screen edge, enabling sub-nanometer precision for optical trapping.
motivation: Optical vortices with intensity zeros are useful for hollow optical traps, but controlling the vortex core position with high precision is challenging.
method: Analytical and numerical modeling of a Laguerre-Gaussian beam diffracted at a rectilinear screen edge, varying screen position, topological charge, wavefront curvature, and screen properties.
result: Regulating the screen edge position with ~1 μm accuracy enables controllable vortex core motion with sub-nanometer accuracy.
conclusion: The proposed method allows precise manipulation of optical hollow traps, which is promising for micro-object trapping and manipulation.

title: Toroidal Transitions In Hydrogenic And Alkali Atoms
authors: Kai Xiang Lee, Vincent Mancois, Kelvin Lim, David Wilkowski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In addition to electric and magnetic multipoles, the expansion of current density also yields toroidal terms, a lesser-known family of multipoles. A recent proposal, I. Kuprov [MATH], Science Adv. 8 abq6751 (2022), explores the possibility of a direct observation of optical toroidal transitions in hydrogen and alkali atoms in the presence of a large magnetic field that decouples the spin and the angular momentum of the electron. However, the difficulty of observing these transitions against the nearby electric dipole (E1) transitions were underestimated because of extra admixture coming from diamagnetic coupling. Here, we revisit the toroidal coupling in atoms, taking diamagnetic contribution into account, and discuss the technical challenges of observing toroidal coupling in atomic physics. We show that toroidal transition should be searched in transitions with low principal quantum numbers. The remaining strong electric-dipole contribution could be removed using an appropriate differential measurement.
tldr: This paper studies toroidal transitions in hydrogenic and alkali atoms, focusing on atomic physics and spectroscopy.
motivation: To revisit the feasibility of observing optical toroidal transitions in atoms, which were previously proposed but underestimated due to diamagnetic coupling.
method: The authors analyze the toroidal coupling in atoms including diamagnetic contributions, and identify transitions with low principal quantum numbers where toroidal effects may be observable.
result: They show that toroidal transitions should be searched in low principal quantum number transitions, and that strong electric-dipole contributions can be removed via differential measurements.
conclusion: Observing toroidal transitions in atoms remains challenging but possible with careful experimental design.

title: Combinatorial Capacity Bounds For The $q$-ary Deletion Channel
authors: Hassan Tavakoli, Thinh Nguyen, Bella Bose
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the \(q\)-ary deletion channel via the pattern-count scalar \(N_n(x,y)\), the number of deletion subsets mapping \(x\in\Sigma_q^n\) to \(y\in\Sigma_q^k\), which factorizes the transition probability. Two sum identities on \(N_n\) certify stochastic normalization and, under uniform input, yield an exact closed-form output entropy. These give the finite-block capacity sandwich \( (1-d)\log_2 q-h_2(d)\;\le\; C_{q,n}\;\le\;(1-d)\log_2 q. \) The exact uniform-input rate is \( {n}I_U(X;Y) =(1-d)\log_2 q+{n}H_{}(n,1-d)-h_2(d)+{n}, \) from which the simpler certified bound \( C_{q,n}\ge (1-d)\log_2 q-h_2(d)+{n} \) follows. The small-\(d\) bound \(C_q(d)\ge\log_2 q+d\log_2 d+O(d)\) follows for all \(q\ge 2\). Numerical experiments at \(n=3,5,10\) and \(q=2,3\) confirm all bounds.
tldr: The paper derives combinatorial capacity bounds for the q-ary deletion channel using pattern-count scalars.
motivation: Understanding the capacity of deletion channels is a fundamental problem in classical information theory, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a pattern-count scalar N_n(x,y) that factorizes the transition probability, and derive sum identities to obtain exact output entropy under uniform input.
result: They obtain finite-block capacity bounds: (1-d)log2 q - h2(d) ≤ C_{q,n} ≤ (1-d)log2 q, and a small-d bound C_q(d) ≥ log2 q + d log2 d + O(d).
conclusion: The bounds are tight for small deletion probabilities and confirmed numerically, but the work is purely classical and not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Bounds And Limitations On Codes Achieving List Recovery Capacity
authors: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Aaron Putterman, Zihan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In coding theory, list recoverability is a fundamental concept which robustly captures how ``spread-out'' codewords are in a code. More formally, given a code [MATH] and input lists [MATH] of size at most [MATH], list recoverability requires that there are at most [MATH] codewords [MATH] such that [MATH] for at least [MATH] choices of [MATH]. List recovery is an important question which has found applications in many areas, including complexity theory, property testing, compressed sensing, streaming algorithms, and cryptography. As our first main result, we establish a tight ``generalized singleton bound''. Formally, we show that for constant [MATH] and sufficiently large alphabets [MATH], if we define [MATH], it is possible for a [MATH] list-recoverable code to have rate [MATH] but impossible to have rate [MATH]. One direction of our result already directly generalizes and improves a weaker impossibility result due to Goldberg, Shangguan, and Tamo. For our second main result, we prove that there is a fundamental shortcoming in existing methods that aim to construct explicit, optimal list-recoverable codes. Indeed, recent work has constructed explicit codes achieving list-decoding capacity (along with other related properties) using a framework introduced in the work of Alon--Edmonds--Luby (AEL). We give a meta-analysis of such constructions by presenting an ``AEL framework'' which captures all such recent constructions in the literature. Within this framework, we show that no AEL-based code can break a recently-identified list-recovery barrier for additive and linear codes.
tldr: This paper establishes tight bounds on list-recoverable codes and shows limitations of existing explicit construction methods.
motivation: List recoverability is a fundamental concept in coding theory with applications in complexity theory, property testing, and cryptography. The paper aims to establish optimal rate bounds and understand limitations of current construction frameworks.
method: The authors prove a tight generalized Singleton bound for list-recoverable codes over large alphabets, and provide a meta-analysis of the Alon-Edmonds-Luby (AEL) framework to show that no AEL-based construction can achieve optimal list-recovery capacity for additive and linear codes.
result: A tight bound showing that for constant input list size and sufficiently large alphabet, the maximum rate is 1 - α - ε, and that AEL-based constructions cannot break a known barrier for additive and linear codes.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits on list-recoverable codes and highlight the need for new construction methods beyond the AEL framework.

title: Learning To Transmit: Volatility-Aware Predictive Communication For Energy-Efficient IoT Networks
authors: John Kangethe, Ifrat Ikhtear Uddin, Longwei Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Communication is the dominant source of energy consumption in Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks, yet many sensed measurements exhibit strong temporal correlations and provide little new information to the receiver. This paper introduces , a volatility-aware predictive communication framework that enables IoT devices to intelligently decide when communication is necessary. Each sensor maintains a lightweight machine learning predictor and transmits only when the prediction residual exceeds an adaptive threshold proportional to the local signal volatility. By normalizing prediction errors using a rolling estimate of signal variability, the proposed transmission policy automatically adapts to changing environmental conditions, seasonal variations, and deployment-specific dynamics without manual threshold tuning. To address long-term non-stationarity, we further propose , an online learning extension based on Recursive Least Squares (RLS) with exponential forgetting, allowing continuous adaptation to sensor drift and evolving signal characteristics. Extensive experiments are conducted on three heterogeneous real-world datasets comprising more than 2.4 million sensor observations from outdoor environmental monitoring, indoor wireless sensor networks, and urban air-quality sensing. Compared with six representative baselines, including periodic transmission, static-threshold suppression, ARIMA, Kalman filtering, EMA, and LMS filtering, achieves up to 94.7\% transmission reduction while maintaining a reconstruction error of 0.352[MATH]C. further reduces reconstruction error by 12--18\% under drift conditions while preserving transmission reduction above 93\%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of volatility-aware predictive communication for energy-efficient and adaptive IoT networks.
tldr: A volatility-aware predictive communication framework for energy-efficient IoT networks that reduces transmission by up to 94.7% while maintaining low reconstruction error.
motivation: Communication is the dominant energy consumer in IoT networks, yet many sensor measurements are temporally correlated and provide little new information, necessitating an adaptive transmission policy.
method: Each sensor uses a lightweight machine learning predictor and transmits only when the prediction residual exceeds an adaptive threshold proportional to local signal volatility; an online learning extension based on Recursive Least Squares with exponential forgetting handles non-stationarity.
result: On three real-world datasets, the framework achieves up to 94.7% transmission reduction with reconstruction error of 0.352°C, and the online extension reduces error by 12–18% under drift while maintaining >93% reduction.
conclusion: Volatility-aware predictive communication is effective for energy-efficient and adaptive IoT networks, significantly reducing transmissions without sacrificing data fidelity.

title: Relative Entropy Analysis Of The Jin-Xin Model: Theory And Numerics
authors: Christina Mahmoud
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work studies the linear Jin-Xin relaxation model by means of the relative entropy method, both at the continuous and fully discrete levels. Under the strict subcharacteristic condition, we obtain an O([MATH]) estimate for the convergence toward the equilibrium transport equation. We then develop discrete relative entropy estimates for a Lie splitting scheme and an asymptotic preserving staggered scheme. A fixed-time analysis further explains the O([MATH]^2 ) behavior observed in the strongly stiff regime and the transition occurring when [MATH] becomes comparable to the time step.
tldr: This paper studies the linear Jin-Xin relaxation model using relative entropy methods at continuous and discrete levels.
motivation: The Jin-Xin model is a hyperbolic relaxation system; understanding its convergence to equilibrium is important for numerical schemes.
method: Relative entropy estimates are derived under the strict subcharacteristic condition for the continuous model and for two numerical schemes (Lie splitting and an asymptotic preserving staggered scheme).
result: An O(ε) convergence rate is obtained for the continuous model, and discrete estimates explain O(ε^2) behavior in the stiff regime.
conclusion: The relative entropy method provides a unified framework for analyzing the Jin-Xin model and its numerical approximations.

title: On Runlength Limited Codes For Bicm Systems
authors: Stephan Zeitz, Florian Roth, Meik D\"orpinghaus, Gerhard Fettweis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the use of runlength-limited (RLL) block codes in bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) systems. In this setting, the RLL code acts as the symbol mapper, whose assignment between input bits and RLL symbols is critical for performance. In this work, we aim at optimizing the assignment scheme of RLL codes. One of the main applications of RLL codes is the mitigation of intersymbol interference (ISI) in systems with coarse quantization. However, channel memory and quantization nonlinearity complicate information theoretic analysis. To enable analytical treatment, we consider a block channel with 1-bit analog-to-digital conversion, modeling the transmission of a single RLL code block. For this channel, we investigate the relationship between the achievable rate in BICM systems-termed BICM capacity-and the RLL code's assignment scheme. Focusing on low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), we derive the optimization problem yielding the optimal assignment scheme. By looking at asymptotically large block-lengths, we infer a practical optimization strategy for RLL codes with finite block-length and channels with inter-block interference. Further, we extend this optimization to two-state RLL (TS-RLL) codes, which offer higher code rates than state independent RLL codes. We demonstrate that optimized TS-RLL codes exhibit significant performance improvements over literature counterparts.
tldr: This paper studies runlength-limited block codes for bit-interleaved coded modulation systems, focusing on optimizing the assignment scheme to improve performance in channels with coarse quantization.
motivation: Runlength-limited codes are used to mitigate intersymbol interference in systems with coarse quantization, but the assignment between input bits and RLL symbols critically affects performance and lacks optimization.
method: The authors model a block channel with 1-bit analog-to-digital conversion and derive an optimization problem for the assignment scheme at low SNRs, extending to two-state RLL codes and finite block-lengths.
result: Optimized assignment schemes for RLL and two-state RLL codes are derived, showing significant performance improvements over literature counterparts.
conclusion: The proposed optimization strategy for RLL code assignment enhances BICM system performance, particularly in low-SNR regimes with coarse quantization.

title: Robust Classification In Ml: A Topological Semantics Approach
authors: Mirko Tagliaferri Dominik Pichler (TU Wien)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust classification is commonly understood as the stability of a classifier under small perturbations (often adversarial) of input data. In this paper, we propose a logical framework for robust classification grounded in topological semantics for modal logic. Evaluation points are feature vectors representing machine-readable objects, and formulas express explicit classifications. Robustness is interpreted geometrically as local truth persistence: a classification is robust at a point if it holds throughout some non-empty open neighbourhood of that point. Building on this perspective, we introduce a logical language with a robustness modality interpreted over S4 topological spaces, together with a robustness-sensitive conditional connective. This conditional connective captures global inclusion relations between robust regions and other properties of the classifier: it holds at a point when the neighbourhood witnessing the robustness of one formula is contained in the truth set of another. In this way, robust classifications can be systematically linked to classification conditions. We provide a sound and complete axiomatisation of the resulting logic. Finally, we introduce Minimal Robust Models, a constructive method for generating models from specified robustness constraints, which yields formal tools for analysing, explaining, and structuring robust classification behaviour.
tldr: This paper proposes a logical framework for robust classification in machine learning using topological semantics for modal logic.
motivation: Robust classification is important for stability under adversarial perturbations, but existing approaches lack a formal logical foundation.
method: The authors introduce a modal logic with a robustness modality interpreted over S4 topological spaces, and define a robustness-sensitive conditional connective to capture global inclusion relations.
result: They provide a sound and complete axiomatization of the logic and introduce Minimal Robust Models for constructing models from robustness constraints.
conclusion: The framework offers formal tools for analyzing and explaining robust classification behavior, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: The authors perform particle-in-cell simulations including radiation reaction to model particle dynamics and coherent emission in magnetized shocks.
result: Radiation reaction significantly alters particle trajectories and reduces the efficiency of coherent emission, leading to observable signatures.
