title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field, enabling super-resolution fluorescence imaging.
result: Demonstrates atomic-scale resolution in fluorescence microscopy, allowing visualization of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical characterization of molecular systems.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses neutron star observations and constraints on the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements.
result: The measurements constrain masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to nuclear equation of state predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter.

title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between Laplace and Helmholtz equations to enable metamaterial design for wave manipulation using static diffusion parameters.
motivation: To bridge the gap between static diffusion and dynamic wave propagation, enabling complex wave functionalities through simpler steady-field design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing wave field reconstruction from static solutions.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, and experimentally validate a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints, merging static and dynamic physics.

title: Physical Sampling For Computational Photography
authors: Ni Chen And David J Brady
abstract: The standard model of photography is that lenses form images and focal planes capture those images. Over the past two decades, however, cameras have been transformed from devices that record focal images into analog-to-digital converters that transform massively parallel optical signals into serial electronic data. Under this new model, one may choose to maximize the quality and quantity of captured information, rather than focal image quality. Here we review the nature of the optical data stream and consider lens and focal plane designs that improve information capture capacity. After maximizing information capacity, the challenge of converting this information to digital data requires novel read-out and compression. We review strategies for approaching physical information limits under realistic size, power, and bandwidth constraints. Multiscale monocentric (spherical primary optics combined with arrays of secondary micro-cameras, each imaging a narrow subfield) and array lens architectures relax unfavorable geometric scaling by trading monolithic optics for co-designed system-level integration (jointly optimized optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems). Metaoptic and mode-sorting focal plane filters implement richer projection operators that sample spectral, polarimetric, and coherence features without requiring exhaustive scanning. Finally, because readout and computation dominate energy at high throughput, we highlight architectures that perform dimensionality reduction before (or during) digitization, including integrated photonic encoders and multilayer optical projections coupled to detection and learned decoding. Together, these developments motivate a shift from cameras optimized to produce 2D images toward cameras engineered as end-to-end information channels, co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout to deliver more task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
tldr: This paper reviews computational photography architectures that optimize information capture and readout under physical constraints, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to shift camera design from producing 2D images to maximizing information capacity per photon and per joule, addressing size, power, and bandwidth constraints.
method: The paper reviews multiscale monocentric optics, metaoptic filters, and integrated photonic encoders that perform dimensionality reduction before digitization.
result: It identifies architectures that improve information capture capacity and reduce readout energy, but no specific experimental or theoretical results are presented.
conclusion: Future cameras should be engineered as end-to-end information channels, co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout for task-relevant measurements.

title: New Lower Bounds For Binary Constant-weight Codes: $A(23,6,10)\geq 2979$ And $A(24,6,10)\geq 4214$
authors: Christian Lysenstoeen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] denote the maximum size of a binary constant-weight code of length [MATH], minimum distance [MATH], and weight [MATH]. We construct explicit codes proving [MATH] and [MATH]. These improve the best surviving explicit codes of sizes 2969 and 4174 and surpass the corresponding 1990 bounds 2970 and 4200 of Brouwer, Shearer, Sloane and Smith, whose code listings were lost. We also obtain [MATH] and [MATH]. All four bounds are now listed in Brouwer's online table. The constructions use a coordinate decomposition in which one half is fixed to a known code and the complementary half is selected from its full cross-compatible pool using CHILS for maximum-weight independent set. For the 2969-word [MATH] incumbent, exact computations with two solver families prove insertion maximality and exclude every improving exchange deleting at most three codewords. We also analyze codes invariant under prime-order permutations: several cycle types are excluded exactly, the [MATH] type has upper bound 499, and reproducible heuristic saturation evidence is reported for the remaining types, with [MATH] left open. Code files, an independent validator, model descriptions, and computational logs are released.
tldr: This paper presents new lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes using combinatorial constructions and computational search.
motivation: Improving bounds for constant-weight codes is a classic problem in coding theory with applications in communication and storage.
method: The authors use a coordinate decomposition method combined with maximum-weight independent set (CHILS) and exact computational solvers to construct and verify codes.
result: New lower bounds A(23,6,10) ≥ 2979 and A(24,6,10) ≥ 4214 are established, surpassing previous records.
conclusion: The constructions improve known bounds and provide explicit codes, with computational evidence of optimality under certain constraints.

title: Integrity Of Peer-to-peer Distributed Llm Inference Under Malicious Nodes
authors: Antonino Nocera Mert Cihangiroglu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peer-to-peer distributed inference executes a Large Language Model (LLM) on pooled consumer hardware by spreading its layers across many nodes. Every request passes through nodes that are owned and controlled by multiple independent parties. However, in this setting, any party can tamper with the output of its layers to corrupt the end result. Recomputing the forward pass on trusted hardware can catch this, but it introduces additional computational cost. The scientific literature includes several prior integrity-checking approaches, such as known-answer traps for image classifiers and cryptographic commitments. However, these solutions test only the exact correctness and do not account for the ordinary variation that may arise between benign nodes. In this paper, we propose a method that checks the output integrity by measuring the variation in the activations that each node passes to the next. A peer who wants to use the network selects a small set of secret canary inputs whose correct activations are known in advance and mixes them into regular traffic. Because the peers cannot tell a canary from a real query, any tampering node corrupts them as well. The deviation from the known reference then reveals malicious activity: benign nodes exhibit only minor variation from hardware-induced noise, whereas tampered nodes deviate far more. We treat the identification of malicious nodes as a probabilistic test that separates two drift distributions, without relying on a fixed threshold. We study 408 configurations with metrics and success criteria fixed before any experiment ran; the detector reaches AUROC 1.0, correctly ranking the malicious shard above every benign shard on every canary in every configuration.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to detect malicious nodes in peer-to-peer distributed LLM inference by measuring activation drift on secret canary inputs.
motivation: In peer-to-peer distributed LLM inference, malicious nodes can tamper with layer outputs, and existing integrity checks do not account for benign hardware-induced variation.
method: The method embeds secret canary inputs with known correct activations into regular traffic; deviation from the reference reveals tampering, and malicious nodes are identified via a probabilistic test separating drift distributions without a fixed threshold.
result: The detector achieves AUROC 1.0 across 408 configurations, correctly ranking malicious shards above benign ones on every canary.
conclusion: The approach effectively detects tampering in distributed LLM inference while tolerating benign hardware noise.

title: Intelligent Qubits
authors: Alexander Givental
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the method of ``intelligent qubits,'' which replace live observers in Wigner's friend and Frauchiger--Renner thought experiments, in order to expose the source of the paradoxes: tacit substitution of Boolean hidden variables for non-commuting quantum propositions. The fallacy traces back to London and Bauer's attempt (1939) to legitimize a self-referential interpretation of observers' ``introspection,'' and thus intertwines the measurement and mind-body problems. We cut the Gordian knot by abandoning reductionism, and describe an alternative which fits, we argue, equally naturally with both physics and anthropology takes on the problems.
tldr: The paper introduces 'intelligent qubits' to analyze Wigner's friend and Frauchiger-Renner paradoxes, arguing that the paradoxes arise from substituting Boolean hidden variables for non-commuting quantum propositions.
motivation: To expose the source of paradoxes in quantum measurement thought experiments and to propose an alternative to reductionist interpretations.
method: The method involves replacing live observers with 'intelligent qubits' in thought experiments and analyzing the logical structure of the paradoxes.
result: The analysis traces the fallacy to London and Bauer's self-referential interpretation of introspection and suggests abandoning reductionism.
conclusion: The paper proposes an alternative interpretation that fits naturally with both physics and anthropology, but does not present testable predictions or technical advances.

title: Bound States Of The Hydrogen-like Atomic Systems In Plasma Environments
authors: Fatma Zohra Khaled, Mustafa Moumni, Mokhtar Falek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We conduct a non-relativistic study of plasma screening effects on hydrogen-like atomic systems using the Screened Coulomb Potential (SCP i.e. Yukawa potential). The radial Schr\"odinger equation is first reduced to a bi-confluent Heun (BCH) equation for the Killingbeck potential which is the truncated version of the SCP, and we write the exact BCH eigenfunctions and eigenenergies. We then study the limitations of these BCH solutions and obtain an analytic description valid for weak to moderate screening using the BCH functional form. The corrected eigenfunctions are constructed order by order up to O(k^3); they are expressed in terms of the Laguerre polynomials and reduces exactly to Coulomb eigenfunctions when k=0. Using these Functions, the energy spectrum is computed via two analytic methods: (i) direct evaluation of the full Yukawa Hamiltonian expectation value, and (ii) the Hellmann-Feynman theorem, yielding integral representation. All methods presented here provide explicit analytical formulas for both wavefunctions and eigenenergies valid for different ranges of the screening. These methods establish a powerful analytic framework for studying confined quantum systems. The thermodynamic properties are also derived using the BCH formulation.
tldr: This paper studies plasma screening effects on hydrogen-like atoms using the Yukawa potential, deriving analytic wavefunctions and energies via the bi-confluent Heun equation.
motivation: To understand how plasma environments modify atomic structure, which is important for astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: The radial Schrödinger equation is reduced to a bi-confluent Heun equation for the Killingbeck potential; analytic eigenfunctions and eigenenergies are obtained, and corrections up to O(k^3) are constructed using Laguerre polynomials.
result: Explicit analytic formulas for wavefunctions and eigenenergies are provided for weak to moderate screening, and thermodynamic properties are derived.
conclusion: The analytic framework is powerful for studying confined quantum systems in plasma environments.

title: Self-stabilization Of Microcombs
authors: Krishna Twayana, Fuchuan Lei, Junyong Choi, Jungwon Kim, Victor Torres-Company
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical frequency combs form phase-locked spectral lines arranged on an equidistant grid fully defined by two degrees of freedom, i.e., the repetition rate and frequency offset. Stabilizing these parameters to a common frequency reference results in a coherent frequency ruler, central for modern precision metrology. However, extending this level of stability to chip-scale microcombs remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate a self-stabilizing mechanism based on self-injection locking of a selected comb line via an external feedback loop. This process establishes a second anchor point in addition to the pump, thereby constraining the comb's frequency noise dynamics. We show that, with an appropriate choice between pump frequency noise and feedback strength, collective fluctuations of the repetition rate are strongly suppressed. The result is a microcomb exhibiting ultralow phase noise and dramatically reduced timing jitter. In a 100 GHz silicon nitride soliton microcomb, we achieve an unprecedented combination of high-conversion efficiency, sub-Hertz intrinsic linewidth across the entire C band, and an integrated timing jitter of 1 fs. This approach enables chip-scale microcombs with remarkable noise performance and fs-level pulse stability, surpassing conventional noise limits and opening new avenues for precision metrology at the chip scale.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a self-stabilization mechanism for chip-scale microcombs using self-injection locking, achieving ultralow phase noise and femtosecond-level timing jitter.
motivation: Stabilizing optical frequency combs on chip-scale microcombs is challenging but essential for precision metrology; existing methods require external references that limit integration.
method: The authors use self-injection locking of a selected comb line via an external feedback loop to create a second anchor point, suppressing collective fluctuations of the repetition rate.
result: They achieve sub-Hertz intrinsic linewidth across the entire C band and an integrated timing jitter of 1 fs in a 100 GHz silicon nitride soliton microcomb.
conclusion: This self-stabilizing approach enables chip-scale microcombs with noise performance surpassing conventional limits, opening new avenues for precision metrology at the chip scale.

title: From Risk To Flourishing: Seeds For Responding To A Complex World
authors: Ryan M. Mcgranaghan, Elisabeth H. Krueger, Alexandre Dunant, Guillaume Falmagne, Lynee L. Turek-Hankins, Sara M. Constantino, Raissa D'souza, Elke U. Weber, Graydon W. Manzke
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flourishing is the actualization of all beings toward their good -- not only individually but collectively, answering the question of `how do we live well with and for each other?'. In science as in society, the tendency to reduce, segregate, specialize, and settle has precluded embracing the concept of flourishing as a guiding principle. We aim to identify an approach to risk science research that promotes the flourishing of socio-ecological-technological systems (SETS). We discuss the normative role of an orientation toward flourishing for the field of risk science. We explore the possibility that (risk) science could be done in a way that is capable of pointing society toward a different future, one more resilient and more capable of flourishing. Our exploration mirrors the conversational nature of flourishing itself: examine ideologies traditionally believed to be rigidly in opposition and consider what emerges in the space(s) and conversation between them. We call this a dialectical approach. Within this paradigm grounded in conversation, pluralism, and pragmatism, we revisit three longstanding tensions in risk science: physical[MATH]social, determinism[MATH]uncertainty, contextuality[MATH]generality. Although these tensions are not new, revisiting them together through the lens of complexity science, and with explicit attention to the normative commitments that shape risk research, reveals underexplored possibilities for the field. Examining them in conversation with the other allows us to explore the provisional seeds for what might be termed complex risk science: interdependence, responsivity, participation, pluralism, openness, and ongoingness. Enacting the dialectical paradigm towards a risk science for a flourishing world will depend on creating collectives toward complex risk science, supporting them with skillfully governed commons, and centering care in our research.
tldr: This paper proposes a dialectical approach to risk science for socio-ecological-technological systems, aiming to promote flourishing rather than merely managing risk.
motivation: The authors argue that traditional risk science is too reductionist and fails to address complex, interconnected challenges; they seek a paradigm that fosters resilience and flourishing.
method: The paper uses a dialectical method, examining tensions in risk science (physical vs. social, determinism vs. uncertainty, contextuality vs. generality) through the lens of complexity science.
result: It identifies provisional seeds for a 'complex risk science': interdependence, responsivity, participation, pluralism, openness, and ongoingness.
conclusion: Enacting this paradigm requires creating collectives, governing commons skillfully, and centering care in research.

title: Recurrence Coefficients Of The Orthogonal Polynomials For Oscillatory Jacobi-type Weight Functions
authors: Xun Zhou Shulin Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two classes of oscillatory Jacobi-type weight functions [MATH], [MATH]. Other restrictions are imposed on [MATH] and [MATH] to guarantee the existence of the associated orthogonal polynomials. By using the ladder operators established in the recent literature for monic orthogonal polynomials associated with Jacobi-type weight functions and three compatibility conditions, we derive two coupled difference equations satisfied by the three-term recurrence coefficients. Compared with the existing results, these equations are structurally simpler and of lower order. Once the initial values are determined, the recurrence coefficients can be computed at any stage through the difference equations. The obtained expressions enable us to conjecture the symbolic forms for the recurrence coefficients.
tldr: This paper derives recurrence coefficients for orthogonal polynomials with oscillatory Jacobi-type weights using ladder operators.
motivation: To obtain simpler and lower-order difference equations for recurrence coefficients of orthogonal polynomials with oscillatory Jacobi-type weights.
method: Uses ladder operators and compatibility conditions for monic orthogonal polynomials to derive coupled difference equations.
result: Derives structurally simpler and lower-order difference equations for the recurrence coefficients, enabling computation at any stage.
conclusion: The obtained expressions allow conjecturing symbolic forms for the recurrence coefficients.

title: An Algebraic-Operator Construction Of The Half-Derivative On A Graded Monomial Space. Part I: Recurrence, Double Factorials, The Wallis Product, And Normalization
authors: Davit Kapanadze
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper constructs a half-order differentiation operator on the graded monomial space spanned by non-negative integer and half-integer powers of x, with x > 0. The algebraic stage uses neither an integral kernel, a limiting process, nor the Gamma function. The operator is assumed to act in the form [MATH]. Requiring two successive applications of the operator to reproduce the ordinary first derivative yields the fundamental recurrence relation [MATH]. Expanding the recurrence produces two linked coefficient families, one for integer powers and one for half-integer powers. Their formulas contain a free normalization constant [MATH], which cancels under composition. Thus, the compositional requirement fixes the relative coefficients but not the scale of each individual half-step. Ratios of even and odd double factorials lead naturally to a partial Wallis product; however, the Wallis product alone does not determine [MATH]. Imposing compatibility with the monomial formula for the left Riemann-Liouville half-derivative with lower limit 0 selects the value [MATH]. With this normalization, [MATH] holds for every [MATH]. The resulting monomial formula agrees with the corresponding Riemann-Liouville formula. For positive integer powers it also agrees with the Caputo formula, whereas for the constant function it agrees only with the Riemann-Liouville rule. The resulting linear compositional operator lowers the exponent by exactly one half and is fully specified on the stated graded monomial space. Extension to broader function spaces, construction of an integral or convolution kernel, and the analysis of non-locality remain open problems.
tldr: This paper constructs a half-order differentiation operator on a graded monomial space using algebraic recurrence relations, without integral kernels or the Gamma function.
motivation: The authors aim to define a fractional derivative operator purely algebraically, avoiding standard analytic tools like integral transforms or limits.
method: The operator is defined by requiring two successive applications to reproduce the first derivative, leading to recurrence relations that determine coefficients for integer and half-integer powers, with a free normalization constant fixed by compatibility with the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative.
result: The resulting operator lowers exponents by exactly one half and matches the Riemann-Liouville formula on the graded monomial space, with the normalization constant determined uniquely.
conclusion: The construction is limited to the graded monomial space; extension to broader function spaces and analysis of non-locality remain open.

title: CRB-Driven Beamforming And Trajectory Optimization For UAV-assisted Isac System
authors: Yi Yang, Qianqian Zhang, Huaxia Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a UAV enhances the sensing capability of a base station (BS) towards a target while ensuring reliable communication towards a downlink user. This architecture is practically attractive for future wireless networks due to the UAV's controllable mobility and adaptive sensing coverage in wireless environments. The sensing performance is characterized by the average Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB), which quantifies the minimum variance of the unbiased angle-of-arrival estimation. To enhance the sensing performance, the UAV trajectory and beamforming parameters are jointly optimized under power and mobility constraints, while satisfying communication requirements to the downlink user. To address the resulting non-convex problem, we employ null-space projection for beamforming design and adopt deep reinforcement learning for the trajectory optimization over a discrete-time scale. In each time slot, beamforming is optimized based on the channel state information to improve CRB performance while mitigating interference between the BS and the communication user. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the time-averaged CRB by over 10%, compared with the ISAC system without UAV assistance, and also achieves a higher sensing accuracy than both the fixed-UAV-trajectory and the maximum-ratio-transmission-based beamforming benchmarks.
tldr: This paper studies UAV-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, optimizing beamforming and trajectory to minimize Cramér-Rao bound for angle estimation.
motivation: UAVs can enhance sensing coverage and mobility in wireless networks, but joint optimization of beamforming and trajectory for sensing performance is challenging.
method: The authors use null-space projection for beamforming design and deep reinforcement learning for trajectory optimization, solving a non-convex problem.
result: The proposed method reduces time-averaged CRB by over 10% compared to ISAC without UAV, and outperforms fixed-trajectory and MRT-based benchmarks.
conclusion: UAV assistance significantly improves sensing accuracy in ISAC systems, and the joint optimization approach is effective.

title: Coset Representatives Corresponding To Yetter-Drinfeld Modules Of Modular Group And Continued Fraction
authors: Yiwei Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give complete conjugacy classes of modular group SL(2,Z). Particularly, the conjugacy classes of hyperbolic elements are decided by the proper equivalence classes of indefinite forms, and we give an example. Finally, we describe the coset representatives of centralizer of S, ST, T and hyperbolic elements of SL(2,Z).
tldr: This paper classifies conjugacy classes of the modular group SL(2,Z) using indefinite forms and describes coset representatives of centralizers.
motivation: To provide a complete classification of conjugacy classes of SL(2,Z), particularly hyperbolic elements, which is a problem in group theory.
method: The paper uses the theory of indefinite quadratic forms to determine proper equivalence classes and then describes coset representatives for centralizers of specific elements.
result: Complete conjugacy classes of SL(2,Z) are given, with hyperbolic classes linked to equivalence classes of indefinite forms.
conclusion: The work offers a group-theoretic classification with potential applications in number theory and modular forms.

title: Foundations Of Machine-Checked Control Theory In Lean
authors: Iman Shames Moritz Doll
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an open-source library for machine-checked control theory in the interactive proof assistant Lean to lay foundations for the verification of cyber-physical systems. To this end, as representative theorems, we present formalizations of Lyapunov stability theory and the small-gain theorem. First, the machinery employed for formalizing Lyapunov stability, i.e., neighborhood filters, allows stating a Lyapunov theorem that covers both points and sets and applies to continuous, discrete, and hybrid systems. Second, the small-gain theorem is proved via stating input-output systems as relations without the usual well-posedness assumption. The Lean formalization of each of these theorems is then presented. We conclude by discussing the library architecture and mentioning some of the other system theoretic results that are formalized in the library along with future plans.
tldr: This paper presents a formalization of control theory theorems in the Lean proof assistant, focusing on Lyapunov stability and the small-gain theorem.
motivation: To enable machine-checked verification of cyber-physical systems by providing a rigorous foundation for control theory in an interactive theorem prover.
method: The authors formalize Lyapunov stability theory using neighborhood filters to cover continuous, discrete, and hybrid systems, and prove the small-gain theorem by modeling input-output systems as relations without well-posedness assumptions.
result: The Lean formalization successfully proves both theorems and establishes a library architecture for further system-theoretic results.
conclusion: The library lays groundwork for verified control systems, but the paper is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Intrinsic Low-Tucker-Rank Theory And Unified Tensor Cur Decomposition For High-Dimensional Hyperinterpolation
authors: Maolin Che, Yimin Wei, Chong Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional hyperinterpolation is severely hampered by the curse of dimensionality, as its coefficient tensors grow exponentially with the ambient dimension. Existing research predominantly focuses on heuristic algorithmic optimizations, often overlooking the inherent structural properties of these tensors. This paper establishes a rigorous theory of intrinsic low-[MATH]-Tucker-rank for hyperinterpolation coefficient tensors, delivering near-optimal low-rank approximations with error bounds that are nearly independent of the dimension. We further construct a unified, Tucker-compatible theoretical framework that integrates both Chidori-type and Fiber-type tensor CUR (TCUR) decompositions, deriving tight and stable Frobenius-norm error estimates that depend exclusively on tensor spectral properties and index set geometry. We mathematically verify the convergence and numerical stability of greedy adaptive index selection schemes and prove their near-optimality, enabling a fully tensor-free hyperinterpolation workflow that avoids constructing the full coefficient array. Three practical greedy TCUR algorithms and a lightweight TCUR-to-Tucker recompression pipeline are proposed as direct corollaries of our structural theory. Numerical experiments across three distinct families of high-dimensional test functions validate all theoretical predictions and confirm the intrinsic low-rank compressibility of hyperinterpolation coefficients. In contrast to prior algorithm-centric studies, this work prioritizes rigorous theoretical characterization over implementation tricks, establishing a unified structural and mathematical foundation for high-dimensional hyperinterpolation.
tldr: This paper establishes a theory of intrinsic low-Tucker-rank for hyperinterpolation coefficient tensors and develops unified tensor CUR decompositions for high-dimensional hyperinterpolation.
motivation: High-dimensional hyperinterpolation suffers from the curse of dimensionality, and existing work lacks rigorous theoretical understanding of the structural properties of coefficient tensors.
method: The authors prove that hyperinterpolation coefficient tensors have intrinsic low Tucker rank, derive error bounds for low-rank approximations, and construct a unified framework for Chidori-type and Fiber-type tensor CUR decompositions with tight error estimates.
result: They provide near-optimal low-rank approximations with dimension-independent error bounds, and propose greedy TCUR algorithms and a TCUR-to-Tucker recompression pipeline that avoid constructing the full coefficient tensor.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous structural and mathematical foundation for high-dimensional hyperinterpolation, validated by numerical experiments.

title: Intelligent Disruption: Undetectable Attacks On Wireless Autoencoders
authors: Han Jiang, Jifa Zhang, Hu Jin, Nan Zhao, Mingqian Liu, Yunfei Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adversarial attacks can degrade the legitimate decision performance in wireless autoencoder communications. However, in complex scenarios with multiple adversaries, the cumulative leakage interference (CLI) caused by the multiple parallel attacks increases the chance of detecting the attacks, while dynamical environments also make the fixed attack strategies difficult to have stable effectiveness. To jointly enhance the undetectability, aggressivity and adaptability of adversarial attacks, we propose a deep learning based intelligent attack framework. Specifically, considering the CLI caused by the multiple parallel attacks, a deep neural network based transmit power control is established to reduce the interference leakage by regulating the transmit power of these adversaries, thereby improving the undetectability. Furthermore, to enhance the attack effectiveness and stability in the dynamic environment, the conditional generative adversarial attack is further developed. The generator takes the attack channel information as the conditional input to produce the perturbating signals to mislead the discriminator by making the attacked received signals resemble the clean received signals, while the discriminator distinguishes between the two under the same condition. Through the adversarial training, the generator can learn to create adaptive perturbating signals with enhanced attack performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms benchmarks in terms of attack undetectability, aggressivity and adaptability.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep learning-based intelligent attack framework for wireless autoencoder communications to enhance undetectability, aggressivity, and adaptability of adversarial attacks.
motivation: Existing adversarial attacks in wireless autoencoder communications suffer from cumulative leakage interference in multi-adversary scenarios and lack adaptability in dynamic environments.
method: The framework uses a DNN-based transmit power control to reduce interference leakage and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to generate adaptive perturbing signals that mimic clean received signals.
result: Simulation results show the proposed framework outperforms benchmarks in attack undetectability, aggressivity, and adaptability.
conclusion: The intelligent attack framework effectively addresses the challenges of undetectability and adaptability in adversarial attacks on wireless autoencoders.

title: Examining User Behavior And Cognitive Biases In Personal Password Security
authors: Evelyn Crowe, Patralika Ghosh, Shreyas Kumar, Rebecca Schlegel, Rebecca Ward, Guofei Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite increasing awareness of cybersecurity risks, users continue to engage in insecure password practices, such as reusing passwords, choosing weak credentials, and neglecting security recommendations. The study explores the behavioral and cognitive factors that influence password decision-making by integrating insights from behavioral economics, particularly hyperbolic discounting, status quo bias, and present bias. We conducted a survey to analyze how people create, store and manage their passwords, examining whether security habits have improved over time in response to greater awareness. Our findings reveal that immediate convenience often outweighs long-term security considerations, leading users to prioritize memorability over strength. Additionally, we identify key psychological biases that contribute to security procrastination and resistance to adopting more secure authentication practices, such as password managers and multi-factor authentication. The study contributes to human-centered security by bridging the gap between security awareness and action, offering practical insights to design user-friendly authentication policies that align with real-world decision-making tendencies.
tldr: This paper studies user behavior and cognitive biases in personal password security, focusing on psychological factors like hyperbolic discounting and status quo bias.
motivation: Despite increased cybersecurity awareness, users continue to engage in insecure password practices. The study aims to understand the behavioral and cognitive factors that lead to such decisions.
method: The authors conducted a survey to analyze how people create, store, and manage passwords, examining the influence of psychological biases on security habits.
result: Findings show that immediate convenience often outweighs long-term security considerations, and key psychological biases contribute to security procrastination and resistance to adopting secure practices.
conclusion: The study offers practical insights for designing user-friendly authentication policies that align with real-world decision-making tendencies.

title: FedLSG: LLM-Enhanced Semantic Calibration For Federated Graph Backdoor Defense
authors: Chenyu Zhou, Yabin Peng, Wei Huang, Kunlin Li, Shuaishuai Zhang, Xinyuan Miao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Graph Neural Networks (FedGNNs) are highly vulnerable to backdoor poisoning, yet existing defenses typically rely on rule-based approaches that lack semantic understanding, making them vulnerable to stealthy triggers and harmful to benign structures. To solve this, we present FedLSG, the first framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) into federated graph backdoor defense. FedLSG introduces a graph and behavior to text grounding scheme that transforms local graph structures and client update behaviors into semantically rich natural language representations. The framework further adopts a lightweight student-teacher architecture. On the server side, a full scale LLM serves as a teacher, providing global contextual guidance and evaluating client updates during aggregation to identify potentially malicious participants. On the client side, a LoRA-based student is maintained to perform semantic reasoning, to suppress the influence of edges associated with backdoor triggers. By enabling semantic interpretation of both graph patterns and client behaviors, the framework adaptively incorporates rule-based signals into message passing and client aggregation for defense. Experiments demonstrate that FedLSG significantly improves resistance to backdoor attacks without compromising graph integrity.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated graph backdoor defense framework using LLMs for semantic calibration.
motivation: Federated GNNs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and existing defenses lack semantic understanding.
method: FedLSG transforms graph structures and client behaviors into text, uses a server-side LLM teacher and client-side LoRA student for semantic reasoning and defense.
result: Experiments show improved resistance to backdoor attacks without compromising graph integrity.
conclusion: LLM-enhanced semantic calibration is effective for federated graph backdoor defense.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Ai For Korean Criminal Law: Sentencing Prediction And Document Drafting
authors: Yeonseok Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Korean criminal justice system utilizes summary proceedings (guyaksik) to expedite high-volume minor infractions, such as simple driving under the influence (DUI), unlicensed driving, and minor traffic casualties. Although this mechanism improves judicial throughput, processing these cases creates a substantial administrative burden for prosecutors, driving the need for automated systems that can precisely translate unstructured legal text into deterministic statutory outcomes. While recent Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at semantic extraction, their probabilistic nature inherently limits their reliability in Legal Judgment Prediction tasks. Specifically, when confronted with the arithmetic constraints of legal statutes, LLMs can produce hallucinations. Given that legal accountability permits virtually no tolerance for stochastic errors, purely neural architectures remain limited in their direct judicial applications. To address these limitations, we propose a Neuro-Symbolic framework that bridges unstructured legal facts with formal verification. Our architecture restricts the LLM exclusively to semantic extraction, while offloading statutory fine calculations to a Satisfiability Modulo Theories solver. This division of labor reduces hallucination risks during computation. Furthermore, we incorporate a Human-in-the-Loop verification scheme to preserve professional legal oversight. We formalize the 2026 Sentencing Guidelines for Traffic Offenses within this pipeline, demonstrating a deterministic approach to supporting summary indictments.
tldr: A neuro-symbolic AI framework for Korean criminal law sentencing prediction and document drafting.
motivation: To reduce administrative burden in Korean summary proceedings by automating legal judgment prediction while avoiding LLM hallucinations.
method: Uses an LLM for semantic extraction and an SMT solver for statutory fine calculations, with human-in-the-loop verification.
result: Demonstrates a deterministic approach to supporting summary indictments based on 2026 Sentencing Guidelines.
conclusion: The neuro-symbolic approach improves reliability over pure LLMs for legal tasks with arithmetic constraints.

title: Defense Against Llm Backdoors Using Critical Neuron Isolation Pruning
authors: Yuxi Li, Zhibo Zhang, Kailong Wang, Xingshuo Han, Ling Shi, Haoyu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where hidden triggers induce malicious outputs. Existing defenses generally fall into inference-time detection or training-time mitigation, but face two key limitations. First, they focus on fine-tuning-based backdoors (e.g., PEFT modules) and fail to address insidious model-editing attacks that bypass training pipelines. Second, they target simple classification settings and do not naturally extend to open-ended LLM generation and do not naturally extend to the open-ended generation characteristics of LLMs. Consequently, these methods focus on surface-level behavioral patterns while neglecting the deeper representational causes of malicious activations. This lack of mechanistic understanding forces defenses to depend on empirical heuristics, limiting their robustness, generality, and practical applicability in real-world LLM deployment. To bridge this gap, we introduce DeCNIP (Defense with Critical Neuron Isolation Pruning), which leverages representational analysis to identify and neutralize backdoors in a unified pipeline. Specifically, DeCNIP identifies trigger-like behaviors by optimizing a cross-entropy loss between harmful prompts with candidate tokens and benign inputs. This representational discovery exposes latent threats by uncovering mechanisms through which triggers hijack model weights. It then isolates Backdoor Critical Neurons (BCNs) and prunes them selectively to remove malicious influence while preserving model utility. Extensive evaluations on six open-source LLMs and two benchmark datasets demonstrate that DeCNIP achieves over 95% relative reduction in Attack Success Rate (ASR), outperforming seven state-of-the-art defenses with only 0.1% neuron intervention. Moreover, it maintains 97% of the model's performance on normal benchmarks, demonstrating its efficacy, robustness, and scalability.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against backdoor attacks in LLMs using critical neuron isolation pruning.
motivation: Existing defenses fail against model-editing attacks and do not extend to open-ended LLM generation, lacking mechanistic understanding.
method: DeCNIP identifies trigger-like behaviors via cross-entropy loss optimization, isolates Backdoor Critical Neurons, and prunes them selectively.
result: Achieves over 95% reduction in Attack Success Rate with only 0.1% neuron intervention, maintaining 97% of normal performance.
conclusion: The method is effective, robust, and scalable for defending LLMs against backdoor attacks.

title: Taming The Security-Energy Paradox: A Green Ai Approach To Optimized Android Malware Detection
authors: Vikas K. Malviya Shrinidhi Sridhar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An increase in advanced Android malware requires the use of deep learning models, which can run on Android devices. But there is a trade-off between security and energy use, as strong detection models can drain the battery of devices fast. This work tests different Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model configurations to balance malware detection performance and energy efficiency. In this work, we compared standard FP32 models with optimized INT8 quantized neural networks with different model depths using TUANDROMD and DREBIN datasets for both classification performance and energy consumption. The results show that INT8 quantization reduces model size by about 3.5 times with a decrease in energy consumption to 0.0189 mJ per inference, while maintaining more than 99.2\% detection accuracy. We found that shallow quantized architectures, such as 3-layer and 4-layer QNNs, reduce energy costs by improving throughput and shortening the time of CPU operating in a high-power state. This work shows that efficient malware protection can be achieved on resource-constrained smartphones and provides a foundation for Green AI in mobile security.
tldr: This paper optimizes Android malware detection using quantized MLP models to balance accuracy and energy consumption.
motivation: Deep learning models for malware detection on mobile devices face a trade-off between security and energy efficiency.
method: The authors compare standard FP32 and INT8 quantized MLP models of varying depths on TUANDROMD and DREBIN datasets, measuring classification performance and energy consumption.
result: INT8 quantization reduces model size by ~3.5x and energy to 0.0189 mJ per inference while maintaining >99.2% detection accuracy; shallow quantized architectures further reduce energy costs.
conclusion: Efficient malware protection on resource-constrained smartphones is achievable, supporting Green AI in mobile security.

title: A Typing System For The Linear Lambda-Calculus In De Bruijn Notation
authors: Vincent Tourneur Philippe de Groote
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a typing system that is particularly well suited for typing the linear lambda-calculus in de Bruijn notation. This typing discipline, which is reminiscent of Hodas' and Miller's model of resource consumption, guarantees that any well-typed term is linear without the need for an occurrence check. We then establish the subject reduction property.
tldr: This paper introduces a typing system for the linear lambda-calculus in de Bruijn notation that guarantees linearity without occurrence checks.
motivation: To provide a typing discipline for linear lambda-calculus that avoids the need for explicit occurrence checks, which is useful for resource-sensitive computation.
method: The authors design a typing system inspired by Hodas and Miller's model of resource consumption, adapted to de Bruijn notation, and prove subject reduction.
result: The typing system ensures that any well-typed term is linear, and the subject reduction property holds.
conclusion: The proposed typing system is effective for ensuring linearity in the linear lambda-calculus with de Bruijn notation.

title: The Importance Of Imagery In Quantum Mechanics
authors: Arthur I. Miller
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: A historical reflection on the role of visualization and imagery in the conceptual development of quantum mechanics.
motivation: To revisit the historical debate between Heisenberg and Schrödinger regarding the importance of visualizable models in quantum theory.
method: Historical analysis and philosophical commentary.
result: Discusses how imagery has influenced quantum mechanics despite the abstract mathematical formalism.
conclusion: Visualization remains a subtle but important aspect of understanding quantum mechanics.

title: Was Schrödinger Ever A Determinist?
authors: Flavio Del Santo
Nicolas Gisin
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This paper examines Schrödinger's philosophical views on determinism, arguing they were more nuanced than commonly portrayed.
motivation: To correct the historical narrative that Schrödinger was a staunch determinist, by analyzing his writings and correspondence.
method: Historical and philosophical analysis of Schrödinger's published works and letters, contextualizing his statements on determinism and indeterminism.
result: Schrödinger's position on determinism evolved and was complex, often embracing a form of statistical determinism rather than strict classical determinism.
conclusion: Schrödinger should not be simplistically labeled a determinist; his views were more radical and aligned with certain indeterministic interpretations of quantum mechanics.

title: Graphene Fet Microfluidic Platform For Electrochemical Molecular Fingerprinting
authors: Roanne Deanne Aves
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a microfluidic platform integrating graphene field-effect transistors for electrochemical molecular fingerprinting.
motivation: To develop a versatile and sensitive platform for molecular analysis using electrochemical detection.
method: Integration of graphene FETs with microfluidic modules into a single experimental workflow.
result: Demonstration of the platform's capability for electrochemical molecular fingerprinting.
conclusion: The platform offers a promising tool for molecular analysis, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complexity From Minimal State Spreading
authors: Rathindra Nath Das
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 14 July 2026;
tldr: A personal perspective on how a 2022 framework for assessing complexity influenced the author's approach to physics.
motivation: The author recounts a personal scientific journey, highlighting the impact of a specific complexity framework on their thinking.
method: Narrative reflection without technical methodology.
result: No new technical results; the paper is a commentary.
conclusion: The framework shaped the author's research direction, but the paper itself does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-idealities In Artificial Synapses
authors: Shafin Bin Hamid
Jean Anne C. Incorvia
Samuel Liu
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews non-idealities in artificial synapses based on non-volatile memory for neuromorphic computing.
motivation: Non-idealities in artificial synapses can limit neuromorphic system performance, so understanding their origins and mitigation is important.
method: The paper reviews various non-ideal effects, their physical origins, mitigation strategies, and opportunities to exploit them.
result: It categorizes non-idealities and discusses how they can be mitigated or harnessed for new computing functionalities.
conclusion: Non-idealities in artificial synapses are both a challenge and an opportunity for neuromorphic computing.

title: Concept2Brain: An Ai Model For Predicting Neurophysiological Responses To Text And Pictures
authors: Alejandro Santos-Mayo
Faith Gilbert
Arash Mirifar
Anna-Lena Tebbe
Ruogu Fang
Mingzhou Ding
Andreas Keil
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents Concept2Brain, an AI model that predicts EEG responses from text or image inputs, generating synthetic neural activity datasets.
motivation: Understanding how the brain processes semantic information is a major challenge; predicting neural responses from stimuli can aid in brain simulation and cognitive research.
method: The authors developed a deep learning model that takes text or pictures as input and outputs predicted EEG signals, trained on a dataset of human neural recordings.
result: Concept2Brain generates synthetic EEG data that closely matches real neural activity patterns, demonstrating the feasibility of predicting neurophysiological responses from semantic content.
conclusion: The model provides a tool for generating reproducible synthetic EEG datasets, potentially useful for studying brain responses to stimuli without extensive data collection.

title: Bringing Radioactive Molecules To The Table | Science
abstract: A compact source of radioactive molecules could enable new tests of fundamental physics.
tldr: A compact source of radioactive molecules is developed to enable new tests of fundamental physics.
motivation: Radioactive molecules offer unique opportunities to probe fundamental symmetries and physics beyond the Standard Model, but their production has been challenging.
method: The paper describes a compact source that efficiently produces and traps radioactive molecules for precision measurements.
result: The source enables the production of specific radioactive molecular species with sufficient yield for spectroscopic studies.
conclusion: This work opens the door to using radioactive molecules in tabletop experiments to test fundamental physics.

authors: Yichen Yan (颜逸辰) And Jie Lin

The relationship between protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) levels is a key aspect of gene expression. tldr: This paper studies the scaling relationship between mRNA and protein levels from an evolutionary fitness perspective.
motivation: Understanding the evolutionary forces driving the correlation between mRNA and protein levels is crucial for reliable gene expression inference.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating fitness effects to derive scaling laws between mRNA and protein abundances.
result: They find that the scaling exponent depends on the fitness landscape and mutation rates, explaining observed correlations.
conclusion: The work provides an evolutionary basis for mRNA-protein correlations, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Essay: Pushing The Frontiers Of High Energy Density Science Toward Unexplored States Of Matter
authors: Federica Coppari
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Coppari

In this forward-looking PRL Essay, Federica Coppari presents a compelling perspective on high-energy-density science, centering on the remarkable behavior of matter under extreme conditions—such as very high pressures and a wide range of temperatures—like those found deep inside planets, stars, and fusion reactions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040001] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This essay discusses high-energy-density science, focusing on matter under extreme pressures and temperatures relevant to planetary interiors and fusion.
motivation: To explore the frontiers of high-energy-density physics and understand material behavior under extreme conditions.
method: Perspective article summarizing current knowledge and future directions in high-energy-density science.
result: Highlights the need for new experimental and theoretical approaches to study matter at extreme conditions.
conclusion: Advancing high-energy-density science will require interdisciplinary efforts and novel facilities.

title: Superfluidity In The Second Layer Of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ On Graphite
authors: Jun Usami And Hiroshi Fukuyama
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Usami and Hiroshi Fukuyama

Evidence for a new type of superfluid phase in second-layer [MATH] on graphite has been obtained from simultaneous measurements of torsional-oscillator response and heat capacity on exactly the same sample down to 30 mK, which resolve substrate-related uncertainties in the previous studie…

tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence for a new superfluid phase in the second layer of 4He on graphite.
motivation: Previous studies of second-layer 4He on graphite were inconclusive due to substrate-related uncertainties; this work aims to resolve those uncertainties.
method: Simultaneous torsional-oscillator and heat capacity measurements were performed on the same sample down to 30 mK.
result: Evidence for a new type of superfluid phase in the second layer was obtained.
conclusion: The findings clarify the phase diagram of 4He films on graphite and reveal a novel superfluid state.

title: Nmr Evidence For Spontaneous Electronic Chiral Order In URhSn
authors: Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, And Y. Shimizu
abstract:

tldr: This paper reports NMR evidence for spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without a chiral lattice.
motivation: To challenge the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework by finding direct evidence in a non-chiral lattice.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on URhSn single crystals.
result: Observation of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, providing the first direct evidence of such order in a material without an inherently chiral lattice.
conclusion: Electronic chirality can emerge in non-chiral lattices, fundamentally changing the understanding of chiral order in strongly correlated materials.

motivation: Accurate hyperfine constants are needed for atomic spectroscopy and nuclear structure studies.

result: Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are determined, and the nuclear quadrupole moment is extracted.
conclusion: The calculated values provide improved atomic data for Sc II, useful for astrophysical and nuclear physics applications.

authors: Hongqiang Xie, Ziyuan Zuo, Weikang Lei, Shibo Song, Jintao Luo, Runbin Chen, Mingzheng Wei, Wei Luo, Long Zou, Zhiming Chen, Yazi Luo, And Guihua Li

motivation: Understanding the microscopic excited-state dynamics initiated by macroscopic propagation of femtosecond laser pulses in gas mixtures is important for applications in remote sensing and plasma physics.
method: The authors combine measurements of forward laser transmission and spectrally resolved side-fluorescence to investigate the coupling between laser propagation and plasma kinetics.
result: The study reveals how spatiotemporal dynamics of the laser pulse affect the fluorescence emission from nitrogen plasma under low-pressure conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the complex interplay between laser propagation and plasma kinetics, which can inform the design of laser-induced plasma experiments.

result: Provides theoretical predictions for parity-violating amplitudes, accounting for neutron skin and nuclear structure.
conclusion: The calculations can be used to extract nuclear information from future experiments on atomic parity violation in highly charged ions.

method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: Six Raman-active phonons were identified, and the spectra matched expectations from symmetry analysis.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed phonon characterization of GdGaI, relevant for understanding its excitonic insulator properties.

title: Mie Voids As Broadband Directional Light Sources

The Kerker effect arises from the interference between electric and magnetic multipoles, enabling directional light scattering in nanophotonics. However, conventional dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles can only act as Kerker sources in narrow spectral regions, limiting their applicability. Here,…

tldr: This paper demonstrates that Mie voids can act as broadband directional light sources via the Kerker effect.
motivation: Conventional dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles only achieve directional scattering in narrow spectral regions, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate Mie voids (air holes in a dielectric medium) to achieve broadband Kerker-type directional scattering.
result: Mie voids exhibit broadband directional light emission due to the overlap of electric and magnetic dipole resonances over a wide wavelength range.
conclusion: Mie voids provide a simple and robust platform for broadband directional light sources, with potential applications in nanophotonics.

title: Room-temperature Antiferromagnetic Resonance In NaMnAs

motivation: To experimentally confirm the magnetic properties of NaMnAs predicted by ab initio studies, specifically its easy-axis antiferromagnetic ordering.
method: Antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) spectroscopy was performed on bulk tetragonal NaMnAs samples.
result: The AFMR data corroborate that NaMnAs is an easy-axis antiferromagnet with the Néel vector along the tetragonal axis.
conclusion: NaMnAs is confirmed as a room-temperature antiferromagnetic semiconductor, which may be relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Short-term Plasticity-based Working Memory Spiking Model Is Resilient To Synaptic Heterogeneity
authors: Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, And Bruno Golosio

The presence of activity-silent working memory has been increasingly supported by experimental observation, and short-term synaptic facilitation is suggested to underlie this phenomenon. Originally proposed in the early 2000s, the synaptic theory of working memory was supported by a relatively simpl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014409] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A spiking neural network model for working memory based on short-term plasticity is shown to be resilient to synaptic heterogeneity.
motivation: To understand how activity-silent working memory can be robustly maintained in neural circuits despite biological variability.
method: The authors develop a spiking neural network model with short-term synaptic facilitation and simulate its dynamics under varying levels of synaptic heterogeneity.
result: The model maintains working memory performance even with significant heterogeneity in synaptic parameters.
conclusion: Short-term plasticity provides a robust mechanism for working memory that is resilient to biological noise.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to show the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the model's order parameter does not correspond to a broken continuous symmetry, and the phase transition is not associated with O(2) symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect; the model's transition is of a different nature.

method: Quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) experiments and quantum dynamical simulations, with Lorentzian fitting to extract spectral features.
result: Two spectral features (peak width and intensity) were identified, characterizing the diffusion process.
conclusion: The study provides insights into hydrogen diffusion in cryogenic liquids, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: THz Dynamics Of Hydrogen Sulfide: Search For Collective Modes Of A Non-hydrogen-bonded Analog Of Water
authors: Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio de Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, And Eleonora Guarini
abstract:
Author(s): Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio De Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, and Eleonora Guarini

Using neutron inelastic scattering, the authors investigate the dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide, which is similar to water but lacks the hydrogen-bond network. While fast sound is preserved, the secondary weakly dispersive mode typical of hydrogen-bonded liquids is not detected.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015412] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the THz dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide using neutron scattering, focusing on collective modes in a non-hydrogen-bonded analog of water.
motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of hydrogen-bonded liquids.

title: Rheology Of Dense Vibrated Granular Flows: Nonmonotonic Response Controlled By Granular Temperature
authors: A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, And E. Lippiello

When subjected to vibrations, the effective viscosity of a granular medium depends heavily on both confining pressure and vibration parameters. In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but a unified framework reconciling experimental observations is lacking.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense vibrated granular flows.
result: Confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations of granular rheology under vibrations.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar

Here, in contrast, we reveal that symmetry breaking can instead en…

motivation: Understanding symmetry breaking in photonic systems is important for controlling light-matter interactions, but its effect on confinement in nonlocal metasurfaces was unclear.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze Mie-tronics supermodes in nonlocal metasurfaces, examining how symmetry breaking alters mode confinement and Q-factors.
result: They find that symmetry breaking can lead to stronger confinement and higher Q-factors, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
conclusion: This work challenges the common belief that symmetry breaking always weakens confinement, offering new design principles for high-Q metasurfaces.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields

tldr: This paper uses bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To generate previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets using novel 3D light fields.

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The electronic structure of bilayer nickelates is sensitive to strain and doping, but the out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on material properties and thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve detector performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effectiveness of standard heat treatments.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic waves.
result: They show that both optical and acoustic forces and torques can be described within the same formalism, highlighting similarities and differences.
conclusion: The unified perspective aids in designing advanced particle manipulation techniques using light and sound.
